# Foundation Stewardship Closure Record v1.0

> Permanent governance artifact. Future auditors may rely on this without re-investigating source.
> Issued by the Enterprise Foundation Stewardship Closure Board · 2026-06-12.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Foundation Baseline | `f5246642c8eee54d35d3cb09ba4e6f3e5abf8c0a` |
| Stewardship Commit | `c0667cc` |
| Scope | P2-T3, P1-H4, P3-D2 (additive foundation controls) |
| Validation | typecheck 0 errors · full suite 167 files / 3107 passed / 0 failed · build pass |
| Freeze Compliance | COMPLIANT — additive only, no frozen model altered |

## State model (every item rated on four independent axes)

| Item | Designed | Implemented | Validated | Operationally Active | Closure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P2-T3** Self-approval prevention | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ **ACTIVE** (runs in `takeWorkflowAction`; all decisions route through it) | **CLOSED** |
| **P1-H4** Identity uniqueness | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ **FULLY ACTIVE** (2026-06-12: 0065 applied to Neon, 71 hashes backfilled, 0 duplicates, 3 unique indexes live, `IDENTITY_UNIQUENESS_ENFORCEMENT=true` local+Vercel, production deployment `o210xdulx` Ready and aliased to avaniishcm.vercel.app) | **CLOSED** |
| **P3-D2** Runtime permission enforcement | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ **ACTIVE** mechanism, enforcing at 3 wired entry points; broad rollout incremental | **CLOSED WITH CONDITIONS** |

---

## P2-T3 — Workflow Self-Approval Prevention

- **Original risk:** a participant could be the decision-maker on their own request — a segregation-of-duties failure that would taint every future approval-bearing program (payroll runs, comp changes, talent actions).
- **Solution:** identity-based SoD guard evaluated before any decision branch in the single approval chokepoint; blocks self-approve, self-reject-from-queue, delegate-to-initiator, delegate-to-self; SYSTEM actor exempt for policy-driven SLA actions.
- **Evidence:** `lib/workflow-guards.ts`; `lib/workflow-engine.ts` guard at decision entry; blocked attempts recorded as `WORKFLOW.SELF_APPROVAL_BLOCKED` in the immutable audit log; all decision UIs/APIs route through `takeWorkflowAction` (verified: no direct step-status writes outside the engine).
- **Tests:** `tests/unit/workflow-self-approval-guard.test.ts` (self/manager/privileged-no-exemption/delegate-abuse/SYSTEM-exempt/no-initiator/source-wiring).
- **Operational dependencies:** none — active on the certified baseline.
- **Residual risk:** none material. **Closure: CLOSED.**

## P1-H4 — Identity Uniqueness Protection

- **Original risk:** duplicate employee identity (Emirates ID, passport, employee code) would corrupt payroll master data, WPS keying, GPSSA records, and any downstream program keyed on a unique worker.
- **Solution:** employee_code case-insensitive uniqueness (app + DB); Emirates ID / passport uniqueness via deterministic keyed HMAC hash columns (encryption-compatible) with partial UNIQUE indexes and in-transaction pre-checks.
- **Evidence:** `lib/identity-hash.ts`, `lib/identity-uniqueness.ts`, schema hash columns, `drizzle/migrations/0065_identity_uniqueness.sql` (additive), `scripts/backfill-identity-hashes.mjs` (guarded, duplicate-count report).
- **Tests:** `tests/unit/identity-uniqueness.test.ts` (determinism, normalisation, additivity, source-wiring, schema).
- **Operational dependencies (ACTIVATION SEQUENCE — REQUIRED for EID/passport):**
  1. Apply `0065` to DEV/UAT via the migration-ledger process (currently `pending`).
  2. Run `scripts/backfill-identity-hashes.mjs REPORT_ONLY=true`; resolve any reported duplicate groups.
  3. Run the backfill in write mode to populate hashes.
  4. Set `IDENTITY_UNIQUENESS_ENFORCEMENT=true` (currently unset).
  5. Record post-apply verification in the ledger.
- **Residual risk:** until the sequence completes, **EID/passport duplicates remain possible** (employee_code duplicates are already prevented). **Closure: CLOSED WITH CONDITIONS** — code complete and validated; EID/passport protection is NOT operationally active.

## P3-D2 — Runtime Permission Enforcement

- **Original risk:** role-only security cannot express per-feature, per-action governance; future programs would each reinvent fine-grained access control or ship gaps.
- **Solution:** `requirePermission()` resolver over the admin-managed `feature_permissions` matrix; runs after (never replaces) `requireRole`; legacy-allow when unconfigured; fail-closed on backend error; cache-coherent on matrix save.
- **Evidence:** `lib/permissions.ts`; wired at `createPerson`, `updatePerson`, `listHistoryEmployees`; `invalidatePermissionCache` on `saveFeaturePermissions`.
- **Tests:** `tests/security/permission-resolver.test.ts` (deny/allow/legacy-allow/non-matrixed/cache/wiring/never-widens).
- **Operational dependencies:** mechanism active. Broad adoption (remaining action surfaces) is incremental; recommend upgrading denial logging to an audit event during rollout.
- **Residual risk:** actions not yet wired rely on `requireRole` alone (their pre-existing posture — no regression). **Closure: CLOSED WITH CONDITIONS** — mechanism complete and enforcing; coverage expands per program.

---

## Future Program Impact

| Program | Status | Rationale |

| Payroll | **SAFE WITH CONDITIONS** | Must complete the P1-H4 activation sequence before payroll master-data load; inherits P2-T3 automatically on its approval flows; wire P3-D2 on payroll actions. |
| Talent / Recruitment / Learning / Succession / Workforce Planning | **SAFE** | Depend on certified identity + approvals; P2-T3 active, P3-D2 mechanism available; no EID/passport-uniqueness dependency at load time. |

| AI Programs | **SAFE** | Continue the governed-read + RBAC pattern; wire P3-D2 on any new privileged capability. |

# KNOWN_GAPS.md — Avaniis HR System

> ⚠️ **STALE DOCUMENT (flagged 2026-06-12).** Content below reflects 2026-05-01 (Sprint 11) and predates ~200 commits: Workflow Intelligence Phases A–D, Migration Factory V2, requirements baseline v1.0, Email Communication Platform, and the effective-dating remediation (Phases 1, 2A–2D). For current gaps use: `docs/qa-qc/00-MASTER-QA-QC-REPORT.md` §7 + `docs/qa-qc/revalidation-2026-06-12.md` (defects), `docs/project-memory/2026-06-04/19-EFFECTIVE-DATING-AUDIT.md` §9 (effective dating), `docs/OPEN-POINTS.md` (deferrals), `CHANGELOG.md` (what shipped).

Last updated: 2026-05-01 (Sprint 11 — Admin Redesign + MDM complete)

---

## Sprint Status

### Sprint 11B — Master Data Management (COMPLETE as of 2026-05-01)

All 9 MDM entities built with full CRUD:
- **Legal Entities, Departments, Positions, Grades, Locations** — full server actions, data table, slide-over drawer, change-reason modal, disable/enable, audit history
- **Work Schedules** — full CRUD + `DayHoursGrid` per-day hours editor
- **Holiday Calendars** — full CRUD + `HolidayCalendarGrid` month-view
- **Leave Types** — full CRUD with UAE Labour Law type restrictions
- **Jobs** — full CRUD with Emiratisation targeting + management role flag
- **Shared MDM component library** — 11 reusable components in `components/mdm/`
- **MDM audit lib** — `lib/mdm-audit.ts` writes change history on every mutation
- **BR guards enforced** — BR-LE, BR-DEPT, BR-POS, BR-GRADE, BR-LOC, BR-WH, BR-LV, BR-JOB series

### Sprint 11A — Admin Panel Redesign (COMPLETE as of 2026-05-01)

- **Grouped sidebar nav** — `config/admin-nav.ts` + `config/manager-nav.ts` replace inline nav; sections: People, Absence, Workflows, Master Data, Access, Settings
- **Feature Permissions** — `app/(hr-admin)/access/feature-permissions/` — toggle per-role feature access; `drizzle/migrations/0012_feature_permissions.sql`; `modules/access/actions.ts`
- **NationalitySelect** — `components/forms/NationalitySelect.tsx` + `lib/data/countries.ts` (200+ countries) replacing plain text input
- **DraftRestoreBanner + useDraftSave** — auto-save form drafts to localStorage with restore prompt on return
- **usePermissions hook** — client-side feature permission resolver
- **Person form helpers** — `lib/person-form-helpers.ts` with 479 unit tests
- **Workflow engine expansion** — `modules/workflow/actions.ts` fully wired step/delegate/approve/reject engine
- **Role-aware middleware** — `middleware.ts` rewritten with RBAC routing guards

### Sprint 2 — Design System (COMPLETE as of 2026-04-29)

All UI pages have been updated to the AVANIIS design system:
- **PILL_TONES status badges** applied consistently across all modules (Absence, Workflows, Org Chart, Settings, Employee Self-Service)
- **Badge component eliminated** — replaced with inline `<span>` tokens throughout; `Badge` import removed from all pages
- **lucide-react icons** — all inline SVG icons replaced; `Eye/EyeOff/Moon/Sun` on login, `Network/Flag/Users` on org chart, `BarChart3/Download/CalendarDays` on absence, `GitBranch/AlertTriangle/Check/X/ArrowRight` on workflows, etc.
- **next/image avatar** — person profile page renders photo from `person.extraData.photoUrl` (jsonb field) with initials fallback
- **Appearance settings** — `settings/appearance/page.tsx` allows per-tenant accent theme, dark mode, and density; SSR hydration applies `data-accent`, `data-dark`, `data-density` to `<body>` via `app/layout.tsx`
- **Design token compliance** — all raw hex removed from `globals.css`; `text-primary-foreground` replaced with `text-white`; scrollbar colours use design tokens
- **Tailwind safelist** — dynamic accent classes protected from purge in `tailwind.config.ts`
- **Full QA/QC audit passed** — Hard Rules 1–7 verified across all 24 modified files

### Sprint 1 — Foundation (COMPLETE)

Foundation, data layer, core HR, and initial UI are built. All module scaffolding is in place.

---

## Ongoing Gaps

This snapshot was taken at the end of Sprint 11 (2026-05-01). The system is in a
**development stage approaching MVP** — foundation, data layer, core HR, design system,
ARIA, absence management, workflow engine, all 9 MDM entities, and admin navigation are
complete. The remaining gaps are primarily payroll calculation, E2E test expansion,
email delivery, and production hardening.

---

## 1. Incomplete / Stub Modules

### Payroll (`modules/payroll/`)
- Schema, types, validations and service stubs are defined.
- **No actual payroll calculation engine** exists yet.
- Integration with external payroll providers (e.g. SAP, ADP) is not implemented.
- Payroll-suspension-on-leave logic is modelled but not fully wired.

### Timesheets (`modules/timesheets/`)
- Module skeleton exists (schema, types, services, validations).
- **No timesheet entry UI** has been built.
- Timesheet approval workflow is not connected.

### GPSSA / UAE Pension
- Compliance calculations for GPSSA (UAE pension scheme) are partially modelled.
- Full contribution calculation and submission reporting is not implemented.
- `tests/unit/gpssa.test.ts` covers the core formula but the production path is incomplete.

---

## 2. Authentication

- **Microsoft Entra SSO** is configured in code but requires an Azure App Registration
  to be set up with real credentials before it works in production.
- The **dev credentials provider** (`DEV_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `DEV_ADMIN_PASSWORD`) must be
  disabled or removed before deploying to production.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) beyond the basic HR-admin / employee split is not yet
  fully enforced across all pages.

---

## 3. Document Vault

- Azure Blob Storage integration (`lib/blob-storage.ts`) is implemented.
- **Local dev fallback** (disk storage) is not implemented — document upload/download
  requires valid Azure credentials even in development.
- Virus scanning / content moderation on uploaded documents is not implemented.

---

## 4. Notifications

- In-app notification system is built.
- **Email delivery** is not connected — there is no SMTP/SendGrid integration.
  `modules/notification/services.ts` writes to the DB but does not send emails.

---

## 5. Org Chart

- `app/(hr-admin)/org-chart/page.tsx` exists.
- The interactive tree visualisation depends on a hierarchy query that needs further
  testing with large datasets.
- No export (PDF/PNG) of the org chart is implemented.

---

## 6. Form Layout Editor

- `app/(hr-admin)/settings/form-layout/FormLayoutEditor.tsx` is built as a UI component.
- Drag-and-drop reordering persistence to the database (`form_configurations` table)
  needs end-to-end verification.

---

## 7. Work Schedules & Delegations

- Work schedules now have full CRUD via the MDM module (Sprint 11B).
- The delegation resolution path in the workflow engine has basic coverage;
  complex multi-level delegation chains are not fully tested.

## 7b. MDM — Remaining Gaps (Post Sprint 11)

- **Seed data not linked to MDM UI** — `drizzle/seed.ts` seeds reference data directly;
  it has not been updated to use the new MDM server actions. New admin-created entities
  are stored correctly but the seed script bypasses business rule guards.
- **RTL layout QA on MDM pages** — Arabic `dir="rtl"` is configured but MDM pages
  (`master-data/*`) have not been visually QA'd in Arabic mode.
- **Soft-delete cascade** — when a Legal Entity is disabled, its child Departments and
  Positions are not automatically disabled. Cascade disable is a Phase 2 item.
- **Grade salary ranges not in MDM** — the `grade_salary_ranges` table (effective-dated
  min/mid/max per grade) has no admin UI; grade ranges are managed via seed data only.
- **Holiday Calendar — Eid estimate handling** — the system stores `is_confirmed = false`
  for estimated Eid dates but there is no notification flow to remind HR to confirm dates
  once officially announced.

---

## 8. i18n Coverage

- English (`messages/en.json`) is well-populated.
- Arabic (`messages/ar.json`) has partial translations — some keys may fall back to English.
- RTL layout is configured via `dir="rtl"` but has not been visually QA'd across all pages.

---

## 9. Tests

- Unit and integration tests cover core business logic well.
- **E2E coverage** (`tests/e2e/`) is minimal — only `persons.spec.ts` exists.
- No visual regression tests.
- Integration tests require a live database; they are not run in CI without a test DB.

---

## 10. CI/CD

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines a GitHub Actions pipeline.
- The pipeline runs lint and type-check but **integration tests are skipped** in CI
  because no test database service is configured.
- No deployment pipeline (CD) is set up yet.

---

## 11. Security Hardening (Pre-Production Checklist)

- [ ] Remove `DEV_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `DEV_ADMIN_PASSWORD` credentials provider
- [ ] Rotate `AUTH_SECRET` and `ENCRYPTION_KEY` for production
- [ ] Enable Content Security Policy headers in `next.config.mjs`
- [ ] Set `secure: true` on session cookies (requires HTTPS)
- [ ] Enable Azure Storage private endpoints (no public access)
- [ ] Add rate limiting to auth endpoints
- [ ] Review and tighten RBAC guards on all server actions

---

## 12. Assumptions Made During Development

- UAE Labour Law rules (annual leave accrual, sick leave limits, etc.) are implemented
  based on Federal Law No. 33 of 2021 as understood at time of development.
  Legal review before production deployment is recommended.
- Hijri calendar conversion uses `@internationalized/date` library — accuracy should be
  validated against official UAE calendar authority outputs for critical date calculations.
- The ARIA AI assistant uses the Anthropic Claude API. Response quality depends on the
  system prompt in `lib/aria/system-prompt.ts` and may require tuning.
- Data retention policies in `lib/retention-policy.ts` are based on assumed regulatory
  requirements. Actual requirements must be confirmed with legal counsel.

# AVANIIS HR — Design Standard

**v1.1 — updated 2026-04-30** (design consistency QA pass — server-component hover pattern, padding rule clarification, What NOT to do expanded, page-in exemption list added)

Extracted from three frozen reference pages:
- `app/(employee)/me/page.tsx` + component tree  
- `components/dashboard/ManagerDashboard.tsx`  
- `components/dashboard/AdminDashboard.tsx`  

These observations are authoritative. Every other page must match.

---

## 1. Shell & Layout Rules

### Page wrapper (outermost div of every page component)

**`(employee)` pages** — layout provides NO padding, so the page wrapper must add its own:
```tsx
<div
  className="page-in"
  style={{
    width: '100%',
    padding: 'calc(24px * var(--density))',
    boxSizing: 'border-box',
  }}
>
```

**`(hr-admin)` pages** — layout already applies `px-6 py-6` (24px), so the page wrapper must NOT add padding:
```tsx
<div
  className="page-in"
  style={{
    width: '100%',
    boxSizing: 'border-box',
  }}
>
```
- **No `maxWidth`**, no `margin: 'auto'`, no `width: Npx`
- `className="page-in"` on every outermost div (triggers `slideInRight 220ms ease`)
- **Components rendered directly as page content** (e.g. `AdminDashboard`, `ManagerDashboard`) must apply `className="page-in"` themselves — they are effectively the page root

### Topbar shell — mandatory element set

Every page across all roles must have ALL five topbar elements. Do not add page-level topbars.

All roles — identical topbar layout:
```
[←]?  [icon] [Page Title]     ←—— Search bar (max-width 400px) ——→     [🔔] [EN/AR] | [Avatar + Name] [logout→]
```

| Element | Component | Spec |
|---------|-----------|------|
| Back button | `ChevronLeft` (16px) | 32×32px; hidden when `pathname === homeRoute` |
| Search bar | inline SVG + span + `<kbd>` | `flex:1; max-width:400px`; centered |
| Bell | inline SVG button | 36×36px; transparent bg |
| Language toggle | `<LocaleSwitcher current={locale} />` | locale read from cookie in server layout |
| User profile | Avatar circle + name + role | Avatar: 36px (admin) / 32px (employee) |
| Logout | `<Link href="/sign-out">` + `<LogOut>` | 32×32px icon; topbar far right; all roles |

**Shell components:**
- `(hr-admin)` → `components/layout/AdminTopbar.tsx` (client). Locale + user props from `app/(hr-admin)/layout.tsx`.
- `(employee)` → `components/employee/EmployeeTopbar.tsx` (client). Locale + user props from `app/(employee)/layout.tsx`.

**Logout placement:** topbar far right on **all roles**. `EmployeeSidebar` footer also retains a logout link as a secondary affordance.

**Do not** hardcode role names or bilingual text in the topbar — derive from `session.user.role`.

### Design coverage
All pages across both route groups (`(hr-admin)` and `(employee)`) follow this standard. There are no remaining exemptions as of 2026-04-30. Sub-pages that were previously deferred (`persons/[id]/**`, `absence/[id]/**`, `absence/new/**`, `absence/rules/**`, `settings/**` sub-pages, `workflows/[instanceId]/**`) have been updated: shadcn Card imports removed, `className="page-in"` applied, page headers converted to inline serif 30px. Residual `space-y-*` and `text-sm` Tailwind helpers within list items are tolerated inside formerly-exempt content areas.

### Full-width two-column layout (where used)
```tsx
// Row container
display: 'flex', gap: 20, alignItems: 'flex-start', width: '100%'

// Left column (main content)
flex: 1, minWidth: 0

// Right column (sidebar/summary)
width: 300  // or 320 for wider right rail
flexShrink: 0
```

### Section spacing
- Between page header and first section: `marginBottom: 24`
- Between KPI grid and two-column layout: `marginBottom: 24`
- Between stacked right-rail cards: `gap: 16`
- Between stacked left cards: `gap: 20`

### Card base
```tsx
background: 'var(--card)'
border: '1px solid var(--border)'
borderRadius: 12
overflow: 'hidden'
```
No `boxShadow`. Border only.

### Card header row
```tsx
padding: '14px 20px'           // employee cards
padding: '16px 20px'           // manager/admin cards
borderBottom: '1px solid var(--border)'
display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between'
```

### Card body
- Default padding: `padding: '20px'`
- Activity/row-based content: `padding: '14px 20px'` per row, no wrapper padding
- Flush table (no padding): `padding: 0`

---

## 2. Typography Rules

| Element | Font | Size | Weight | Color | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page title | `var(--font-serif)` | 30–32px | 500 | `var(--ink-1)` | letter-spacing `-0.5px` to `-0.6px`; margin 0 |
| Page subtitle | `var(--font-sans)` | 14px | 400 | `var(--ink-3)` | margin 0 |

## 4. Color Usage Rules

| Usage | Token |

| Page background | `var(--bg)` — #F0F2F5 |

## 5. Interaction & Animation Rules

### Page entry
```css
/* Already in globals.css */
@keyframes slideInRight {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(12px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}
.page-in { animation: slideInRight .22s ease; }
```
Every page outermost div **must** have `className="page-in"`.

### Modal entry
```css
/* Already in globals.css */
@keyframes modalIn {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px) scale(0.98); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}
```

### Row hover

**Server Component pattern** (no `'use client'` — cannot use event handlers or `useState`):
```tsx
// Use Tailwind pseudo-class alongside inline styles:
<tr
  className="hover:bg-surface"
  style={{ transition: 'background 120ms', background: 'transparent' }}
>
```

**Client Component pattern** (with `'use client'`):
```tsx
// Option A — useState:
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
<tr
  style={{ background: hovered ? 'var(--surface)' : 'transparent', transition: 'background 120ms' }}
  onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)}
  onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(false)}
>

// Option B — inline event handlers (simpler for single rows):
<tr
  style={{ transition: 'background 120ms' }}
  onMouseEnter={e => (e.currentTarget.style.background = 'var(--surface)')}
  onMouseLeave={e => (e.currentTarget.style.background = '')}
>
```
Only add hover on rows that are **actually clickable** or expandable.

### Button hover
All buttons must use CSS transitions `120ms`. Use `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` or CSS `:hover` for:
- Primary → `background: var(--accent-700)`
- Secondary → `borderColor: var(--ink-4)`
- Ghost → `background: var(--surface)`
- Danger → `background: #FBE9E9`

### Progress bar fill
```tsx
transition: 'width 0.4s ease'  // observed in LeaveBalanceBand
```

### Cursor
- `cursor: 'pointer'` — every button, link, clickable row, clickable card
- `cursor: 'default'` — non-interactive rows (never pointer on static rows)

---

## 6. Spacing Scale

| Value | Usage |
|---|---|
| 2px | hairline gap between sub-elements |
| 4px | tight inline gap (flex-direction column subtitle gap) |
| 6px | pill internal gap, small button gap |
| 8px | form gap, KPI icon+label gap |
| 10px | button group gap, hero button gap |
| 12px | table th padding vertical, list item gap |
| 14px | card header padding vertical, row padding vertical |
| 16px | standard grid gap, stacked right-rail gap |
| 20px | card body padding, two-column gap |
| 24px | section margin-bottom, page header margin-bottom |
| 28px | hero padding (28px 32px) |
| 32px | hero padding horizontal |

---

## 7. What NOT to do

- ❌ `boxShadow` on cards — border only
- ❌ `maxWidth` on page wrapper divs
- ❌ `margin: 'auto'` on page wrapper divs
- ❌ Arabic text / bilingual labels displayed in any hr-admin page UI — English only
- ❌ `dir="rtl"` rows showing Arabic DB fields (`nameAr`, `fullNameAr`, etc.) in hr-admin tables
- ❌ Arabic `labelAr` values in `MANAGER_NAV` or `HR_ADMIN_NAV` sidebar entries
- ❌ Tailwind classes mixed with inline styles on pages (existing Tailwind in shell components is grandfathered — new page code must use inline styles)
- ❌ Tailwind `bg-accent-050 text-accent-700` as a status pill (it's an accent tint, not a status) — use `var(--status-approved-*)` for APPROVED/ACTIVE states
- ❌ Tailwind `bg-red-50 text-red-700/800` as a status pill — use `var(--status-rejected-*)`
- ❌ Tailwind `bg-status-warning-bg text-status-warning-fg` as a status pill — use `var(--status-pending-*)` inline style
- ❌ Hardcoded `#hex` colors for status pills — use `var(--status-...)`
- ❌ shadcn `<Card>` / `<CardContent>` / `<CardHeader>` / `<CardTitle>` in redesigned list/index pages — use inline-style div equivalents
- ❌ Grey (`#9CA3AF`, `bg-accent-100 text-accent-700`) as avatar background — use `AVATAR_PALETTE` colors
- ❌ Raw text empty states ("No data available" with no icon treatment) — use 48px icon circle + serif title pattern
- ❌ `cursor: pointer` on non-clickable rows
- ❌ Missing `className="page-in"` on page outer div (except documented exemption list above)
- ❌ `padding: 'calc(24px * var(--density))'` on `(hr-admin)` page wrappers — double-padding with layout
- ❌ No padding on `(employee)` page wrappers — layout provides none, page must add it
- ❌ `border-radius` values other than: `4px` (progress bars), `6–7px` (buttons/small), `8px` (icon squares), `12px` (cards), `14px` (modals), `50%` (avatars), `999px` (pills)

# Enterprise Email Communication Platform — Deployment & Operations Notes

> Added 2026-06-06. Provider-agnostic (Microsoft Graph API **or** SMTP),
> admin-configurable, multi-tenant-ready email platform for AVANIIS HCM.

## What shipped

| Area | Location |
|---|---|
| DB schema | `drizzle/schema/communication.ts` (5 tables) |
| Migration | `drizzle/migrations/0062_email_platform.sql` |
| Provider abstraction | `modules/communication/providers/{types,graph,smtp}.ts` |
| Email service | `modules/communication/email-service.ts` |
| Orchestrator | `modules/communication/orchestrator.ts` |
| Templates | `modules/communication/templates/{render,base-layout,seeds}.ts` |
| Action tokens | `modules/communication/action-tokens.ts` (reuses `workflow_email_tokens`) |
| Server actions | `modules/communication/actions.ts` |
| Admin UI | `app/(hr-admin)/settings/communication/` |
| Dispatch cron | `app/api/cron/email-dispatch/route.ts` (+ `vercel.json`) |
| Approval handler | `app/api/workflow/action/route.ts` (extended: provider channel + branded page) |
| Leave email wiring | `modules/absence/actions.ts` → `submitLeaveRequest` (non-blocking) |
| Audit channel | `lib/audit.ts` (+ `EMAIL_GRAPH`, `EMAIL_SMTP`) |
| Tests | `tests/unit/communication-platform.test.ts` |

## Architecture (hard rule)

`Business event → NotificationOrchestrator → EmailService → selected provider`.
Business logic never calls a provider directly. Email is **queued** in
`email_messages` and delivered asynchronously by the cron dispatcher, so a
provider outage can never block or roll back the originating transaction
(e.g. leave submission).

## Migration deployment (manual — Neon)

The Drizzle journal only tracks 0000–0039; **0062 is a manual migration**.
DB safety rails (`guard-db-write.js`) intentionally block automated writes to Neon.

1. Open the Neon SQL Editor (Test environment first).
2. Paste & run `drizzle/migrations/0062_email_platform.sql` (idempotent —
   `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, enums guarded with `DO $$ … EXCEPTION`).
3. Verify the 5 tables + enums exist, then repeat in Production.
4. No change needed for `audit_log.channel` — it is `varchar(30)` with no CHECK
   constraint, so the new `EMAIL_GRAPH` / `EMAIL_SMTP` values are TS-side only.

No `email_action_tokens` table is created — the existing `workflow_email_tokens`
table is reused for approve/reject links.

## Environment variables

| Var | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | AES-256-GCM for provider secrets | **reused** (already set) |
| `WORKFLOW_JWT_SECRET` | Signs email approval tokens | **reused** (already set) |
| `CRON_SECRET` | Authorises the dispatch cron | **reused** (already set) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | Base URL for approval links | should be set (defaults to `https://hr.avaniis.ae`) |

**No new env vars are required.** Provider credentials (Graph tenant/client/secret,
SMTP host/user/password, endpoints) are stored **in the database, encrypted**, and
configured from the Administration UI — not via env. The legacy env-driven sender
in `modules/employee-letters/email.ts` is untouched and independent.

## Cron schedule

`vercel.json` adds `/api/cron/email-dispatch` every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`).
- Accepts `GET` (Vercel Cron) and `POST`; both require `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}`.
- **Idempotent under concurrency**: each message is claimed via an atomic
  `QUEUED → SENDING` conditional update (`WHERE status='QUEUED' RETURNING`), so
  overlapping dispatch runs can never double-send a message.
- On Vercel Hobby plan, cron is limited to daily — adjust the schedule or run on a
  Pro plan / external scheduler if 5-minute cadence is required.

## Configuration steps (admin)

1. Administration → Settings → **Communication Settings**.
2. Fill the **Graph API** and/or **SMTP** tab → Save (secrets are encrypted; the
   field shows `••••••••` afterwards — leave it to keep, retype to rotate).
3. Set **Sender Defaults** (per-module from-addresses).
4. **Test Email** tab → send a test → provider is marked *Tested* on success.
5. **Provider** tab → **Activate** the tested provider (only one active at a time).
   - Activation requires a PASSED test, unless a SUPER_ADMIN supplies an override
     reason (audited).

## Security notes

- Secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (`*_enc` columns); never returned to the
  browser (page strips them, exposes only boolean "configured" flags).
- Provider execution is server-only (`import 'server-only'`); credentials never
  reach client JS.
- Approval links: HMAC-signed, single-use (atomic `used_at` claim), time-bound
  (`exp`), nonce (`jti`). Decisions flow through `takeWorkflowAction` — RBAC,
  wrong-approver rejection, completed/reassigned/cancelled invalidation, and
  idempotency are all enforced by the existing engine.
- All config changes, activations, test attempts, template edits, retries and
  email approval decisions are written to the immutable audit log; email decisions
  carry channel `EMAIL_GRAPH` / `EMAIL_SMTP`.
- Email queue failures in leave submission are caught and logged — they never roll
  back or block the leave request; missing manager work email simply skips email.

## Multi-tenant / global readiness

`email_provider_settings` and `email_sender_defaults` carry `tenant_id` +
nullable `legal_entity_id`. Today one global active config is used; the resolver
(`getActiveProviderRow`) is tenant-scoped so per-legal-entity providers, regional
sender domains, and language-specific templates (`email_templates.language_code`)
can be layered in without schema changes.

## Verification performed

- `pnpm typecheck` → 0 errors.
- `pnpm build` → success; `/settings/communication`, cron, and action routes compiled.
- `pnpm vitest run tests/unit/communication-platform.test.ts` → 15/15 passed.
- Regression: `absence-services` + `approval-notification-detail` → 35/35 passed.

### Remaining manual verification (needs a configured provider + DB)
- End-to-end: submit leave → `email_messages` QUEUED row to manager work email →
  cron dispatch → SENT; click Approve → workflow APPROVED + branded confirmation +
  audit row with `EMAIL_GRAPH`/`EMAIL_SMTP`; reused/expired token rejected.
- UI light/dark contrast pass on `/settings/communication`.

# Leave (Absence) Balances — Enterprise Redesign Functional Specification

> **Status:** DRAFT — pending review/approval. **No application code to be modified until this is approved and the code freeze is lifted.**
> **Page:** Absence → Balances (`/absence/balances`)
> **Source file:** `app/(hr-admin)/absence/balances/page.tsx`
> **Export route:** `app/(hr-admin)/absence/balances/export/route.ts`
> **Author / date:** Redesign session 2026-06-05
> **Related rules:** CLAUDE.md Non-Negotiable Rules 4 (bilingual), 6 (barrels), 7 (CSS tokens), 10 (nav sync); RBAC entity-scoping.

---

## 0. Purpose & Background

The current page exposes a single **Year** dropdown plus an **"Apply"** button and renders one flat, unbounded grid of `absence_balances` rows for the selected year (per person × leave type × year), with an inline server-rendered accrual-history drill-down.

### Why "Apply" exists today
The page is a **Server Component** with no client reactivity. The Year `<select>` lives in a native HTML `<form>`; a native form cannot change the URL until submitted, so **"Apply" is simply the form submit button** — it reloads the page with `?year=<value>`, the server re-queries, and the grid re-renders. With one filter it is redundant; with ten filters it becomes a usability hazard (users change filters and forget to submit).

### Decision
**Remove "Apply"; filters auto-apply.** See §1.

### Business objective
Enable HR, Operations, Payroll, Finance, and Management to analyze leave balances by legal entity, department, project, employee, leave type, and date range — supporting workforce planning, leave-liability monitoring, expiry management, and operational reporting.

---

## 1. Final UX Behavior

### 1.1 Layout (top → bottom)
1. **Page header** — title "Absence Balances", live row count, actions: `Download CSV`, `Reset filters`. *(A `Columns` show/hide toggle is **out of Phase 1 scope** — deferred as a future enhancement.)*
2. **Summary cards strip** — 5 cards (§4). Each card reflects the **currently filtered** result set, and clicking a card applies its corresponding filter (e.g. "Negative Balances" → Balance Status = Negative). **Responsive wrapping:** cards lay out in a single row on wide screens and wrap to a 2-up grid on tablets and a 1-up stack on narrow/mobile screens (CSS flex/grid `wrap`, min card width ~180px) — never horizontally scroll or overflow.
3. **Filter bar** — responsive grid of the 10 filters (§2), in a panel that is collapsible on small screens.
4. **Active filter chips** — below the bar, one chip per non-default active filter (e.g. `Department: Finance ✕`); clicking ✕ clears that single filter. A `Clear all` shortcut mirrors `Reset filters`.
5. **Grid** — existing columns + drill-down, with status color cues and a sticky header.

### 1.2 Auto-apply rules
- **Dropdown / discrete filters** (Legal Entity, Department, Project, Leave Type, Balance Year, Balance Status, Carry-Forward Status) → **apply instantly on change**.
- **Free-text & date filters** (Employee search, Start Date, End Date) → **debounced 300–400 ms**, with in-flight request cancellation.
- **No "Apply" button.** A **`Reset filters`** control restores all defaults.
- Filter state is encoded in the **URL query string** (shareable / bookmarkable / back-button safe) — preserves the existing server-component model.

### 1.3 Empty states (must be distinct)
- **No data for year:** "No balance rows yet for {year}. They are created on first accrual." (existing copy).
- **Filters excluded everything:** "No balances match your filters." + a `Clear filters` CTA. (New — prevents users misreading an over-filtered view as "no data".)

### 1.4 Defaults
| Filter | Default |
|---|---|
| Legal Entity | All Entities (within RBAC scope) |
| Department | All Departments |
| Project | All Projects |
| Leave Type | All Leave Types |
| Employee | (empty) |
| Balance Year | Current year (`new Date().getUTCFullYear()` UTC) |
| Start Date / End Date | (empty) |
| Balance Status | All |
| Carry-Forward Status | All |

---

## 2. Filter Definitions, Business Meaning & Source

| # | Filter | Business meaning | Data source | Type |
|---|--------|------------------|-------------|------|
| 1 | **Legal Entity** | Which UAE legal entity the balance belongs to. Liability and reporting are entity-scoped. | `absence_balances.legal_entity_id` → `legal_entities` | Dropdown, RBAC-scoped |
| 2 | **Department** | Org-unit the employee currently belongs to. For org-structure analysis. | `worker_assignments.department_id` (current rows) | Dropdown |
| 3 | **Project** | Project/cost-centre the employee is assigned to. For project-level workforce/liability. | `worker_assignments.project_id` (current rows, nullable) | Dropdown |
| 4 | **Leave Type** | Annual, Sick, etc. For type-specific accrual/liability analysis. | `absence_balances.absence_type_id` → `absence_types` | Dropdown |
| 5 | **Employee** | Specific person, by name (EN/AR) or employee number. | `persons.full_name_en` / `full_name_ar` / `person_number` | Searchable typeahead |
| 6 | **Balance Year** | The accrual year the balance snapshot belongs to. | `absence_balances.balance_year` | Dropdown (year−2 … year+1) |
| 7 | **Start Date** | Lower bound of the **system/activity date range** (see §2.1). | derived (see §2.1) | Date input (debounced) |
| 8 | **End Date** | Upper bound of the system/activity date range. | derived (see §2.1) | Date input (debounced) |
| 9 | **Balance Status** | Health of the closing balance. | derived from `closing_balance_days` + carry-forward expiry | Dropdown |
| 10 | **Carry-Forward Status** | State of carried-forward days. | derived from `carried_forward_days`, `forfeited_days`, expiry | Dropdown |

### 2.1 Start Date / End Date — "System Date Range" (CONFIRMED)
Start/End Date filter the **balance record's own system/activity dates**, NOT leave-request or leave-transaction dates.

A balance row matches if **any** of the following falls within `[Start Date, End Date]`:
- `created_at` — when the balance row was created
- `updated_at` — when it was last modified/recalculated
- `last_accrual_date` — when monthly accrual last ran for it

Business reading: *"Show balances that were created, updated, recalculated, or accrued within this range."* Useful for auditing recent accrual runs, recalculations, and data-load activity. Either bound may be supplied alone (open-ended range).

> **Explicitly excluded:** these dates are NOT the leave dates an employee took. A separate "Leave Liability / Transactions" report would cover taken-leave-by-date (out of scope here, see §11 Phase 3 note).

### 2.2 Balance Status values
| Value | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Positive** | `closing_balance_days > 0` |
| **Negative** | `closing_balance_days < 0` |
| **Zero** | `closing_balance_days = 0` |
| **Expiring Soon** | `carried_forward_days > 0` AND the **derived** carry-forward expiry date is within **90 days** of "today" (UTC) AND not yet forfeited. Expiry date is computed, not stored — see expiry-resolution note below. |

> `closing_balance_days` is the application-computed stored value: `opening + accrued + carriedForward + adjusted − taken − pending − forfeited`. NULL closing is treated as "not yet computed" and excluded from Positive/Negative/Zero buckets (shown only under "All").

> **Carry-forward expiry resolution (APPROVED — see §12 Decision #1).** `absence_balances` has **no** `carry_forward_expiry_date` column; expiry is derived as `balanceYearStart + carryForwardExpiryMonths`.
> - **Phase 1 — plan-level approximation:** JOIN `absence_types.absence_plan_id → absence_plans` and use `absence_plans.carry_forward_expiry_months` as the effective expiry window. Expiry date = `make_date(balance_year, 1, 1) + carry_forward_expiry_months months`; "Expiring Soon" = that date within 90 days of today (UTC); `carry_forward_expiry_months = 0` means **never expires** (never Expiring Soon). This is computed purely in SQL via the plan JOIN — no per-person resolution.
> - **Phase 2 — exact per-person resolution:** replace the plan-level value with the per-person × per-type resolved rule from `resolveLeaveRuleSet` (`lib/leave-rule-resolver.ts`), which scores rule sets by legal entity, entity type, nationality category, and employment type (default = 24 months, BR-AL-003). **No new `carry_forward_expiry_date` column is to be added in Phase 1.**

### 2.3 Carry-Forward Status values
| Value | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Eligible** | `carried_forward_days > 0` AND the **derived** expiry date is in the future (not yet forfeited) |
| **Not Eligible** | `carried_forward_days = 0` (nothing carried) |
| **Expired** | `forfeited_days > 0` (carry-forward lapsed / forfeited) |

> "Eligible" uses the **same expiry-resolution approach** as "Expiring Soon" (§2.2):
> - **Phase 1:** plan-level expiry via the `absence_plans.carry_forward_expiry_months` JOIN; `0` months = never expires → always Eligible while `carried_forward_days > 0`.
> - **Phase 2:** exact per-person expiry via `resolveLeaveRuleSet`.
> "Not Eligible" (`= 0`) and "Expired" (`forfeited_days > 0`) are pure SQL on stored columns in both phases — no expiry resolution needed.

## 3. UX Detail — Filter Bar Components
- **Dropdowns** styled with design tokens only (`var(--card)`, `var(--border)`, `var(--ink-1)` …) — never raw hex (Rule 7).
- **Employee typeahead:** async, RBAC-scoped, `LIMIT 20`, matches name (EN/AR) + person number; shows `personNumber · fullNameEn`.
- **Bilingual labels:** every filter label and option must have `_en` and `_ar` (Rule 4). AR is auto-translated via the existing `lib/translation.ts` framework where applicable.
- **Chips:** render only for non-default values; each chip clears just its own filter; `Clear all` = Reset.
- **Accessibility:** all inputs labelled; date inputs keyboard-navigable; color cues paired with text/badges (not color alone).

---

## 4. Summary Card Definitions

All cards aggregate over the **same filtered WHERE clause** as the grid (one extra grouped query, run in parallel with the rows query).

| Card | Definition | Query |
|---|---|---|
| **Total Employees** | Distinct persons in the filtered set. | `COUNT(DISTINCT person_id)` |
| **Total Available Leave Days** | Sum of positive closing balances (leave still available). **Day-count metric — NOT a monetary liability value.** | `SUM(GREATEST(closing_balance_days, 0))` |
| **Expiring Leave Days** | Carry-forward **days** expiring within 90 days (day count, not money). Uses the §6.3 Phase 1 plan-level expiry predicate. | `SUM(carried_forward_days)` WHERE expiry within 90 days AND not forfeited |
| **Negative Balances** | Count of balance rows where closing < 0 (over-taken / data issues). | `COUNT(*)` WHERE `closing_balance_days < 0` |
| **Pending Leave Impact** | Total pending (requested-not-yet-approved) **days** that will reduce available balances. | `SUM(pending_days)` |

- **All card figures are day counts, not monetary amounts.** No daily-rate or salary valuation is applied here. Monetary leave-liability valuation is explicitly **out of scope** for this page and deferred to the Phase 3 "Leave Liability" report (§10). Card labels must read in "days" so HR/Finance never mistake them for currency values.
- Each card is clickable → applies its natural filter (Negative Balances → Balance Status = Negative; Expiring Leave Days → Balance Status = Expiring Soon; Pending Leave Impact → sorts by `pending_days DESC`, per §12 Decision #4 — no dedicated pending status filter in Phase 1).
- Cards must show "—" / 0 gracefully on empty result sets.
- **Responsive layout:** single row on wide screens → 2-up on tablet → 1-up stacked on narrow/mobile (flex/grid wrap, min card width ~180px); cards never overflow or horizontally scroll.
- Numbers formatted with `var(--font-mono)` for figures, consistent with the grid.

---

## 5. Edge Cases

1. **NULL `closing_balance_days`** — not yet computed; excluded from Positive/Negative/Zero, included under "All". Card sums treat NULL as 0.
2. **Multiple current assignments (CONFIRMED: match any)** — Department/Project filter matches if ANY current assignment matches; results **de-duplicated** so each `absence_balances.id` appears exactly once (`SELECT DISTINCT` on balance id, or `EXISTS` subquery to avoid join fan-out).
3. **No assignment at all** (e.g. terminated mid-year) — balance still exists; appears under "All Departments/Projects" but is excluded when a specific Department/Project is selected.
4. **Nullable Project** — persons with no project: excluded by a specific Project filter; included under "All Projects".
5. **Over-filtered → empty** — distinct empty-state message + Clear CTA (§1.3).
6. **RBAC scope vs Entity filter** — a non-SUPER_ADMIN selecting an entity they don't own must get nothing (server enforces scope first; entity dropdown is pre-scoped so this shouldn't be selectable).
7. **Crafted `?expanded=` param** — existing protection retained: only expand if the row is in the in-scope result set (prevents cross-entity probing).
8. **Year out of range** — existing Zod clamp `min(2000) max(3000)`, default current year; retained.
9. **Open-ended date range** — Start only, or End only, both valid.
10. **Expiry date unavailable** — fall back to plan standard expiry month (§2.3 note); never crash the status computation.
11. **Large result sets** — pagination required (§7); cards aggregate the full filtered set, not just the visible page.
12. **Timezone** — "today" and year boundaries computed in **UTC** (consistent with existing `getUTCFullYear()`); date filters compared as `date` (no time component).
13. **Export vs grid divergence** — export MUST inherit the exact filter set (§8); otherwise a filtered grid + unfiltered CSV silently disagree.

---

## 6. Query Logic

### 6.1 Base (direct filters — no schema change)
```
FROM absence_balances ab
  LEFT JOIN persons p       ON ab.person_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN absence_types t ON ab.absence_type_id = t.id
WHERE ab.tenant_id = :TENANT_ID
  AND ab.balance_year = :year
  [AND ab.legal_entity_id = :entityId]            -- filter 1 / RBAC scope
  [AND ab.legal_entity_id = :scopedEntityId]      -- forced for non-SUPER_ADMIN
  [AND ab.absence_type_id = :typeId]              -- filter 4
  [AND (p.full_name_en ILIKE :q OR p.full_name_ar ILIKE :q OR p.person_number ILIKE :q)]  -- filter 5
  [AND <balance status predicate>]                -- filter 9 (SQL, not JS)
  [AND <carry-forward status predicate>]          -- filter 10 (SQL)
  [AND (ab.created_at::date BETWEEN :start AND :end
        OR ab.updated_at::date BETWEEN :start AND :end
        OR ab.last_accrual_date BETWEEN :start AND :end)]  -- filters 7/8 system date range
ORDER BY p.person_number ASC, t.type_code ASC
LIMIT :pageSize OFFSET :offset
```

### 6.2 Department / Project (Phase 2 — join, match-any, de-dup)
Use `EXISTS` to avoid join fan-out and the need for `DISTINCT`:
```
AND EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM worker_assignments wa
  WHERE wa.person_id = ab.person_id
    AND wa.tenant_id = ab.tenant_id
    AND wa.is_current = true
    [AND wa.department_id = :departmentId]   -- filter 2
    [AND wa.project_id   = :projectId]       -- filter 3
)
```
- `EXISTS` guarantees each balance row appears once even with multiple current assignments (match-any semantics satisfied without duplicate rows).

### 6.3 Status predicates (must be SQL, never post-fetch JS)
- Positive: `ab.closing_balance_days > 0`
- Negative: `ab.closing_balance_days < 0`
- Zero: `ab.closing_balance_days = 0`
- CF Not Eligible: `ab.carried_forward_days = 0`
- CF Expired: `ab.forfeited_days > 0`

**Expiry-dependent predicates (Expiring Soon, CF Eligible) — APPROVED phased approach (§12 Decision #1):**

*Phase 1 — plan-level expiry via JOIN (pure SQL, no per-person resolution):*
```
JOIN absence_plans pl ON t.absence_plan_id = pl.id
-- effective expiry date for the row (NULL/0 months => never expires):
-- expiry := make_date(ab.balance_year, 1, 1) + (pl.carry_forward_expiry_months * INTERVAL '1 month')

-- Expiring Soon:
ab.carried_forward_days > 0
  AND ab.forfeited_days = 0
  AND pl.carry_forward_expiry_months > 0
  AND (make_date(ab.balance_year,1,1) + pl.carry_forward_expiry_months * INTERVAL '1 month')::date
        BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND (CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '90 days')

-- CF Eligible:
ab.carried_forward_days > 0
  AND ab.forfeited_days = 0
  AND ( pl.carry_forward_expiry_months = 0   -- never expires
        OR (make_date(ab.balance_year,1,1) + pl.carry_forward_expiry_months * INTERVAL '1 month')::date > CURRENT_DATE )
```
> `make_date`/`CURRENT_DATE` evaluated in UTC to match §5.12. `carry_forward_expiry_months = 0` ⇒ never expires (always Eligible while carried > 0; never Expiring Soon).

*Phase 2 — exact per-person expiry:* substitute the plan-level `carry_forward_expiry_months` with the per-person × per-type value resolved by `resolveLeaveRuleSet` (`lib/leave-rule-resolver.ts`). Because resolution is per-row contextual (entity/nationality/employment type), this is computed in the app/batch layer rather than a single SQL JOIN. **No `carry_forward_expiry_date` column is added in Phase 1.**

### 6.4 Summary aggregates (parallel query, same WHERE)
```
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT ab.person_id)                          AS total_employees,
  SUM(GREATEST(ab.closing_balance_days, 0))             AS total_available_days,
  SUM(CASE WHEN <expiring soon> THEN ab.carried_forward_days ELSE 0 END) AS expiring_days,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ab.closing_balance_days < 0)   AS negative_balances,
  SUM(ab.pending_days)                                  AS pending_impact
FROM absence_balances ab ... <same joins/WHERE minus pagination>
```
> `<expiring soon>` reuses the **§6.3 Phase 1 plan-level expiry predicate** (JOIN `absence_plans`); Phase 2 swaps in the per-person resolved value. `total_available_days` and `expiring_days` are **day counts**, not monetary values (§4).

### 6.5 Indexes (Phase 2 migration — next clean slot **0065** as of 2026-06-12; verify folder before assigning)
- `absence_balances (tenant_id, balance_year, legal_entity_id, absence_type_id)` — composite for the common filtered path.
- Ensure `worker_assignments (person_id, is_current)` (and ideally `(department_id)`, `(project_id)`) are indexed for the EXISTS subquery.
- **No schema column changes required.** All filters map to existing columns.

## 7. Performance Considerations
- **Pagination required** — current page fetches all rows for the year unbounded (~500 employees × ~8 types ≈ 4,000 rows). Add server-side pagination (keyset preferred, or LIMIT/OFFSET).
- **Debounce** employee/date filters (300–400 ms) + cancel in-flight to avoid request storms from auto-apply.
- **Parallelize** rows query + summary aggregate query (`Promise.all`).
- **SQL-side filtering** for status / carry-forward (never fetch-then-filter — would break counts, cards, and pagination).
- **Cache** filter option lists (entities/departments/projects/types) — they change rarely; fetch server-side at render and pass as props.
- **EXISTS over JOIN+DISTINCT** for dept/project to avoid fan-out.
- Server-component model retained; if filter interactivity feels sluggish at scale, isolate only the filter bar as a small client island that pushes state to the URL via `router.replace`.

---

## 8. Export Behavior
- **Current:** `/absence/balances/export` accepts only `year`.
- **Required:** export MUST accept and apply the **full active filter set** (entity, department, project, leave type, employee, year, start/end date, balance status, carry-forward status) so the CSV equals the on-screen grid.
- Export is **RBAC-scoped identically** to the page (no broader data than the user can see on screen).
- Export ignores pagination (exports the full filtered set) and includes the same columns **plus the computed `Balance Status` and `Carry-Forward Status` label columns — these are REQUIRED, not optional** (Payroll/Finance reconciliation depends on them). The computed columns use the same §6.3 logic as the grid (Phase 1 plan-level expiry).
- Filenames should encode the year and key filters for traceability (e.g. `absence-balances_2026_entity-X.csv`).

---

## 9. Security / RBAC Considerations
- Allowed roles unchanged: `HR_ADMIN`, `HR_DIRECTOR`, `PAYROLL_ADMIN`, `MANAGER`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `FINANCE`; others redirected to role home.
- **Entity scope is enforced server-side first:** non-`SUPER_ADMIN` users are forced to `legal_entity_id = session.user.legalEntityId`. The Legal Entity dropdown is pre-scoped so out-of-scope entities are not selectable.
- **Employee typeahead API** must call `auth()` + role check and be entity-scoped (cannot enumerate persons outside scope).
- **Filter option lists** (departments/projects/entities) must be scoped — never leak other entities' org structure.
- **Drill-down protection retained** — expand only in-scope rows (anti-probing).
- Page is **read-only** → no `db.transaction`/`audit.log` writes, no PII decryption beyond what's already displayed. No new PII surfaced (names/numbers already shown). Confirm no encrypted fields are added to filters/export.
- **`tenant_id`** enforced on every query (Rule 9).
- All new user-facing strings **bilingual** (Rule 4); if nav changes, update **both** `config/workspace-nav.ts` and `config/admin-nav.ts` (Rule 10).

## 10. Phase 1 & Phase 2 Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — High value, low risk (NO schema change)
1. Remove "Apply"; implement auto-apply (instant dropdowns; debounced employee/date) via URL params.
2. Add `Reset filters` + active-filter chips + distinct empty states.
3. Add **direct filters:** Legal Entity (RBAC-scoped), Leave Type, Balance Year (existing), Balance Status, Carry-Forward Status, Employee search (typeahead API).
4. Add **summary cards** (5) with parallel aggregate query; cards clickable to apply filters.
5. Make **CSV export inherit filters**.
6. Status/carry-forward predicates implemented in SQL.
7. Bilingual labels; tokens-only styling.

### Phase 2 — Structural
1. **Department + Project filters** via `worker_assignments` EXISTS subquery (match-any, de-dup).
2. **System date-range filter** (created_at / updated_at / last_accrual_date).
3. **Pagination** (keyset/LIMIT-OFFSET).
4. **Index migration** at the next clean slot (**0065** as of 2026-06-12 — §6.5; verify folder before assigning). WIP `_wip_` migrations 0055–0057/0060 are NOT applied; 0061 status unrecorded; 0062–0064 ARE applied to DEV/UAT (ledger SSOT: `docs/environment/migration-ledger.test.md`).
5. Confirm carry-forward **expiry date** derivation from absence-plan rules for "Expiring Soon"/"Eligible".

### Phase 3 — Optional (separate report, out of current scope)
- "Leave Liability" analytics: monetary valuation `closing_balance_days × daily rate` per entity/department/project; taken-leave-by-date transactions report. Recommended as its own page rather than overloading this grid.

## 11. QA Test Scenarios

### Functional
1. Default load → current year, All filters, grid + cards populate; no "Apply" button present.
2. Change Leave Type dropdown → grid + cards update **instantly**, no submit.
3. Type in Employee search → updates after debounce; matches by EN name, AR name, and person number.
4. Set Start/End date → after debounce, only balances whose created/updated/last_accrual fall in range appear; verify open-ended (start-only, end-only).
5. Balance Status = Negative → only closing < 0 rows; Negative Balances card count matches grid count.
6. Balance Status = Expiring Soon → only carry-forward expiring within 90 days, not forfeited.
7. Carry-Forward Status = Expired → only `forfeited_days > 0`.
8. Department filter (Phase 2) → person with 2 current assignments in matching dept appears **once** (no duplicate rows).
9. Project filter (Phase 2) → person with null project excluded; "All Projects" includes them.
10. Reset filters → all defaults restored, URL cleared, cards recomputed.
11. Active chips → each chip's ✕ clears only its filter; Clear all = Reset.
12. CSV export → downloaded rows exactly match the on-screen filtered set (including dept/project/date/status filters).
13. Empty due to filters → "No balances match your filters" + Clear CTA (distinct from "no data for year").
14. Drill-down still expands accrual history for in-scope rows.

### RBAC / Security
15. HR_ADMIN (entity-scoped) cannot see or select other entities; URL-tampering `legal_entity_id` of another entity returns nothing.
16. Employee typeahead never returns out-of-scope persons.
17. Department/Project option lists scoped to caller's entity.
18. Crafted `?expanded=<other-entity-row>` does not expand.
19. EMPLOYEE / disallowed roles redirected to role home.

### Performance
20. 4,000-row dataset → first paint within target; pagination limits payload.
21. Rapid filter changes → debounced, in-flight requests cancelled, no request storm.
22. Summary aggregate query runs in parallel (not serial) with rows query.
23. Status/dept filters resolved in SQL (verify via query log — no full-table fetch then JS filter).

### Data correctness
24. Card sums tie out to manual SUM over filtered rows (available days, expiring days, pending).
25. NULL closing_balance handled (excluded from P/N/Z, counted as 0 in sums).
26. UTC year/today boundaries (no off-by-one at month/year edge).

## 12. Open Items — Decision Table

> **STATUS: APPROVED 2026-06-05.** All items below are confirmed decisions (not open proposals). The "Recommended decision" column now records the **approved** decision. Implementation must follow these.

> **Schema finding (verified 2026-06-05, read-only):** `absence_balances` has **no carry-forward expiry-date column**. Expiry is computed at runtime as `balanceYearStart + carryForwardExpiryMonths` (`computeCarryForwardExpiry`, `modules/absence/services.ts:106`). `carryForwardExpiryMonths` is **resolved per person × leave type** via `resolveLeaveRuleSet` (`lib/leave-rule-resolver.ts:236`), which scores rule sets by legal entity, entity type, nationality category, and employment type. Default rule = **24 months** (BR-AL-003); most other rule sets = **0** (never expires). `absence_plans.carryForwardExpiryMonths` (foundation.ts:830) exists but is only the plan-level fallback, not necessarily the effective value for a given person.

| # | Item | Current assumption in spec | Risk if not confirmed | Recommended decision | Build impact |
|---|------|---------------------------|----------------------|---------------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Carry-forward expiry source** for "Expiring Soon" / "Eligible" / 90-day window | §2.3/§6.3 originally implied a simple SQL predicate on stored fields | **HIGH** — expiry is per-person resolved, not a column; a naive SQL `WHERE` would be wrong (wrong/zero employees flagged → liability mis-stated). Pure-SQL filtering as originally written is **not achievable**. | **APPROVED.** **Phase 1 — plan-level approximation:** JOIN `absence_types.absence_plan_id → absence_plans` and use `absence_plans.carry_forward_expiry_months`; expiry = `make_date(balance_year,1,1) + carry_forward_expiry_months months`, compare to `CURRENT_DATE + 90d`; `0` months = never expires. **Phase 2 — exact per-person resolution** via `resolveLeaveRuleSet` (app/batch layer), after deeper rule-resolution support. **No `carry_forward_expiry_date` column is added in Phase 1.** | Phase 1: extra JOIN to `absence_plans`; status predicate is a date expression. Phase 2: app-layer per-person resolution (no schema column in Phase 1). Affects §2.2, §2.3, §6.3, §6.4, card "Expiring Leave Days". |
| 2 | **Carry-forward CF "Eligible" definition** | "carried_forward_days > 0 AND expiry in future" | MEDIUM — same per-person expiry dependency as #1 | Same approach as #1 (plan-level in Phase 1). "Not Eligible" (`= 0`) and "Expired" (`forfeited_days > 0`) are safe as pure SQL. | Inherits #1. |
| 3 | **Pagination style & page size** | §7 says keyset preferred, else LIMIT/OFFSET | LOW — both work; offset is simpler but slower deep in large sets | LIMIT/OFFSET, default **50 rows/page**, for Phase 1 simplicity; revisit keyset only if datasets exceed ~10k rows. | Minor; both Server-Component friendly. |
| 4 | **"Pending Leave Impact" card interaction** | §4 says clickable; unclear if it filters | LOW — cosmetic | Card displays `SUM(pending_days)`; clicking sorts by `pending_days DESC` (no dedicated status). No pending-only filter in Phase 1. | Trivial. |
| 5 | **Migration slot number** | §6.5/§10 originally assumed **0058** | MEDIUM — WIP `_wip_` migrations 0055–0057/0060–0061 exist unapplied; collision risk | **APPROVED.** Do **not** hard-code 0058. Re-check the latest migration number by listing `drizzle/migrations/` at **Phase 2 build time** and take the next free slot. | Phase 2 only; no Phase 1 impact. |
| 6 | **"Match any current assignment" + `is_current` semantics** | §6.2 uses `wa.is_current = true` | MEDIUM — for terminated/historical staff, `is_current` may exclude them entirely; "current" vs "during balance year" diverge | **APPROVED.** Department/Project filters use **current assignments only** (`is_current = true`), **match-any** (balance appears if ANY current assignment matches the selected Department/Project), with **de-duplication** so each balance row appears once (via `EXISTS`). Terminated/inactive employees appear **only when filters are set to All**, unless they still have a current assignment record. | Phase 2; matches existing assignment model. |
| 7 | **Half-pay / no-pay leave types in liability sums** | "Total Available Leave Days" sums all positive closings | MEDIUM — summing no-pay/half-pay days alongside full-pay overstates monetary liability | Phase 1: card counts **days** (not money), so summing is acceptable; label as "days", not "liability value". Defer monetary valuation to Phase 3 liability report. | None Phase 1; clarify card label. |

---

*End of specification. Awaiting review/approval before lifting code freeze.*

## 3. Condition Builder Component

```
Component: ConditionBuilder
Reused in: StepEditorDrawer (step activation), GroupEditor (dynamic membership)
Props: {
  value:    Condition[]
  logic:    'AND' | 'OR'
  onChange: (conditions: Condition[], logic: 'AND' | 'OR') => void
  context:  'LEAVE' | 'SALARY' | 'TRAVEL' | 'ATTENDANCE' | 'EMPLOYMENT_ACTION' | 'ANY'
}

Visual Layout:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Match [ALL ▼] of the following conditions:                  │
│                                                              │
│  [Leave type ▼] [is ▼] [Annual Leave ▼]              [✕]   │
│  [Leave days ▼] [greater than ▼] [_7_______]          [✕]   │
│                                                              │
│  ┌── Or any of: (group) ────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  [Grade level ▼] [≥ ▼] [_7_]                   [✕]  │   │
│  │  [Is UAE national ▼] [is true ▼]                [✕]  │   │
│  │  [+ Add condition]                                    │   │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                              │
│  [+ Add condition]    [+ Add group (AND/OR)]                 │
│                                                              │
│  ── Human-readable preview ─────────────────────────────    │
│  "Activates when: leave type is Annual AND leave days >      │
│   7 AND (grade level ≥ 7 OR is UAE national)"                │
│                                                              │
│  [▶ Test with values]  → opens test panel                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Field Picker (searchable dropdown, grouped by category):

  EMPLOYEE
    Grade code           (TEXT)
    Grade level          (NUMBER)
    Department           (REFERENCE)
    Entity               (REFERENCE)
    Nationality          (TEXT/ENUM)
    Nationality category (ENUM: UAE_NATIONAL / GCC / EXPAT)
    Employment type      (ENUM)
    Service months       (NUMBER)
    Service years        (NUMBER)
    Is on probation      (BOOLEAN)
    Is UAE national      (BOOLEAN)
  
  LEAVE REQUEST
    Leave type           (ENUM)
    Duration (days)      (NUMBER)
    Working days         (NUMBER)
    Is backdated         (BOOLEAN)
    Backdated days       (NUMBER)
    Balance remaining    (NUMBER)
    Balance % used       (NUMBER)
    Start month          (NUMBER 1-12)
    Spans Ramadan        (BOOLEAN)
  
  SALARY CHANGE
    Increment %          (NUMBER)
    New basic salary     (NUMBER)
    Current basic salary (NUMBER)
    Increment amount     (NUMBER)
  
  TRAVEL
    Destination country  (TEXT ISO-3)
    Is international     (BOOLEAN)
    Duration (days)      (NUMBER)
    Estimated cost (AED) (NUMBER)
    Is GCC country       (BOOLEAN)
  
  ATTENDANCE
    Correction type      (ENUM: PUNCH_IN/PUNCH_OUT/BOTH)
    Missed days          (NUMBER)
    Is repeated this month (BOOLEAN)
  
  EMPLOYMENT ACTION
    Action type          (ENUM: PROMOTE/TRANSFER/GRADE_CHANGE)
    Salary impact %      (NUMBER)
  
  SYSTEM
    Today's date         (DATE)
    Day of week          (NUMBER 0-6)
    Current month        (NUMBER 1-12)
    Is Ramadan period    (BOOLEAN)

Operator options per data type:

  TEXT/ENUM:  is / is not / is one of / is not one of / contains / starts with
  NUMBER:     = / ≠ / > / < / ≥ / ≤ / between
  BOOLEAN:    is true / is false
  DATE:       is / before / after / between / in the last N days
  ARRAY:      contains / does not contain / is empty / is not empty

Test Panel (when [▶ Test with values] clicked):

  "Enter test values to see result:"
  
  Leave type:       [Annual Leave ▼]
  Leave days:       [8]
  Grade level:      [5]
  Is UAE national:  [No ▼]
  
  Result: ✓ TRUE (conditions met)
  
  Detail:
  ✓ leave type is Annual: TRUE
  ✓ leave.days (8) > 7:   TRUE
  ✗ Grade (5) ≥ 7:        FALSE
  ✗ UAE national:         FALSE
  → Group OR: FALSE (none matched)
  
  Final: TRUE AND TRUE AND FALSE = FALSE
  Wait — re-read: top-level is "ALL" (AND)
  → leave.type AND leave.days AND (grade OR nationality)
  → TRUE AND TRUE AND FALSE = FALSE
```

```
     APPROVED  ·  29 May 2026 at 14:30  ·  "Approved, enjoy"
     Via: Line Manager Hierarchy · N+1
  
  ▶  Step 2 — Head of Department (YOU: Khalid Al Rashidi)
     ACTIVE  ·  SLA: 22 working hours remaining
     Via: Line Manager Hierarchy · HOD level
     Condition met: leave.days (8) > 7
  
  ○  Step 3 — HR Admin
     PENDING (activates after Step 2)
     Condition: leave.days > 14 [NOT MET at current duration]
  
  ⊘  Step 4 — SKIPPED
     HR Admin special types step
     leave.type (ANNUAL) not in [MATERNITY, HAJJ, ...]
  
  ⚙  Step 5 — System Auto-Action
     Deducts balance, creates calendar block
  
  ── ACTION ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  
  Comment (required for rejection):
  [                                                        ]
  [                                                        ]
  
  [← Send back to Step 1]   [→ Request info]
  
         [✕ Reject]                [✓ Approve]
  
  [→ Delegate to colleague]
    Delegate to: [person picker]
    Reason: [text]
    [Confirm Delegation]
```

## 7. Employee Request Status View (`/me/requests/[requestId]`)

```
Component: MyRequestStatus

"Your leave request — Annual Leave (8 days)"
Submitted: 29 May 2026  ·  Status: [IN PROGRESS 🔵]

  ✓  Step 1 — Line Manager (Omar Haddad)
     Approved  ·  29 May 2026 at 14:30
     "Approved, enjoy your trip"
  
  ⏳ Step 2 — Head of Department (Khalid Al Rashidi)
     Pending  ·  SLA expires: 02 Jun 2026 at 14:00 GST
  
  ○  Step 3 — HR Admin
     Waiting (activates after Step 2)
  
  ⊘  Step 4 — SKIPPED
     (This step applies to Maternity / Paternity / Hajj leave types)
  
  ⚙  Step 5 — System: Process leave
     (Activates automatically after all approvals)

"Estimated approval: by 02 Jun 2026 (assuming no delays)"

[Withdraw request] (only available while in Step 1)
```

**Design note:** Full transparency — employee sees all approver names and step conditions. This differs from Oracle HCM which hides future approvers. Our approach builds trust in UAE workforce culture where employees expect to understand the process.

## 10. Design System Compliance

Per `DESIGN-STANDARD.md`:

**`(hr-admin)` pages** — layout provides `px-6 py-6` already:
```tsx
<div className="page-in" style={{ width: '100%', boxSizing: 'border-box' }}>
```

**Color tokens** (no raw hex):
```tsx
// SLA status colors
// Green:  text-[var(--success)] / bg-[var(--success-muted)]
// Amber:  text-[var(--warning)] / bg-[var(--warning-muted)]
// Red:    text-[var(--destructive)] / bg-[var(--destructive-muted)]

// Status badges use PILL_TONES:
// ACTIVE:     'success'
// PENDING:    'warning'
// REJECTED:   'destructive'
// APPROVED:   'success'
// SKIPPED:    'muted'
// ESCALATED:  'warning'
```

**Icons** (lucide-react only):
```tsx
import {
  Clock,        // SLA / time
  CheckCircle,  // Approved
  XCircle,      // Rejected
  AlertTriangle,// Overdue / warning
  ArrowRight,   // Active step indicator
  SkipForward,  // Skipped step
  Settings,     // Auto step
  Users,        // Custom group
  User,         // Named person / line manager
  Building,     // Position hierarchy
  Shield,       // HR Admin / elevated
  GitBranch,    // Workflow definition
} from 'lucide-react'
```

**Arabic (RTL) support:**
- All user-facing strings have `nameAr` counterparts
- `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` when language = AR
- Pipeline layout mirrors in RTL (step 1 on right, last step on left)
- All date/time displays use UAE locale format: `DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm GST`

## Server Actions, TypeScript Types, and Integration Contracts

**Status:** Design — Awaiting Implementation Approval

## 1. TypeScript Types

```typescript

// ── Error Types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export class WorkflowPreSubmitError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public guard:   string,    // e.g., 'HAJJ_ELIGIBILITY', 'LEAVE_BALANCE'
    public message: string,
    public ruleRef: string,    // e.g., 'BR-HJ-002'
    public data?:   Record<string, unknown>
  ) { super(message) }
}

export class WorkflowVacancyError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public positionId:    string,
    public positionTitle: string,
    public policy:        string   // 'BLOCK_WITH_ERROR'
  ) { super(`Cannot route: position ${positionTitle} is vacant and no fallback configured`) }
}

export class WorkflowUnauthorizedError extends Error {
  constructor(public message: string) { super(message) }
}
```

## 2. Server Action Interfaces

### 2.1 `submitWorkflow`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Submit a request into a workflow.
 * Captures immutable hierarchy + context snapshots.
 * Resolves the full approval chain upfront.
 * Activates the first step and sends notifications.
 * 
 * Throws WorkflowPreSubmitError if any pre-submit guard fails.
 */
export async function submitWorkflow(input: {
  workflowCode: string
  entityType:   string     // e.g., 'absence_entries'
  entityId:     string     // UUID of the record being approved
  initiatorId:  string
  context:      WorkflowContext
  comments?:    string
}): Promise<{
  instance:      WorkflowInstanceV2
  resolvedSteps: ResolvedStep[]
  slaDeadline:   Date
}>
```

### 2.2 `takeWorkflowAction`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Actor takes an action on their assigned workflow step.
 * Advances the workflow to the next step (or completes it).
 * Triggers downstream effects on final approval.
 * 
 * Throws WorkflowUnauthorizedError if actor is not the assigned approver.
 */
export async function takeWorkflowAction(input: {
  instanceStepId: string
  actorId:        string
  action:         'APPROVE' | 'REJECT' | 'SEND_BACK' | 'REQUEST_INFO' | 'DELEGATE'
  comments?:      string
  delegateToId?:  string  // required when action = 'DELEGATE'
  sendBackToStep?: number // required when action = 'SEND_BACK'; step_order to send back to
}): Promise<{
  updatedStep:   WorkflowInstanceStep
  nextStep:      WorkflowInstanceStep | null
  instanceStatus: string
}>
```

### 2.3 `previewWorkflow`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Preview what the approval chain would look like for a given employee + context
 * WITHOUT creating a workflow instance.
 * 
 * Used in:
 *   - Employee "Your request will go to..." info before submitting
 *   - HR Admin Hierarchy Preview Tool in workflow builder
 *   - Testing workflow configuration changes
 */
export async function previewWorkflow(input: {
  workflowCode: string
  initiatorId:  string
  context:      WorkflowContext
}): Promise<WorkflowPreview>
```

### 2.4 `getPendingApprovals`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Get paginated list of pending approval steps for an approver.
 * Scoped to their assigned steps only.
 * Includes SLA status, hierarchy type, employee context.
 */
export async function getPendingApprovals(input: {
  approverId: string
  filters?: {
    module?:        string
    entityId?:      string
    hierarchyType?: HierarchyType
    overdueOnly?:   boolean
    search?:        string  // employee name search
  }
  pagination: PaginationInput
  sortBy?: 'OLDEST_FIRST' | 'SLA_EXPIRING' | 'NEWEST'
}): Promise<PaginatedResult<PendingApprovalItem>>
```

### 2.5 `getWorkflowInstance`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Get full workflow instance detail including all steps and audit log.
 * Used for:
 *   - Employee request status view
 *   - Approver detail drawer
 *   - HR Admin workflow monitoring
 * 
 * context_snapshot and hierarchy_snapshot are returned ONLY for HR_ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN.
 */
export async function getWorkflowInstance(input: {
  instanceId: string
  actorId:    string
}): Promise<{
  instance:          WorkflowInstanceV2
  steps:             WorkflowInstanceStep[]
  auditLog:          WorkflowAuditLogEntry[]
  hierarchySnapshot: HierarchySnapshot | null  // null unless HR Admin
  contextSnapshot:   WorkflowContext | null     // null unless HR Admin
}>
```

### 2.6 `cancelWorkflow`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Cancel an in-progress workflow.
 * Allowed by: initiator (if still in Step 1) or HR_ADMIN (any stage).
 */
export async function cancelWorkflow(input: {
  instanceId:  string
  cancelledBy: string
  reason:      string
}): Promise<void>
```

### 2.7 `createDelegation`

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * Create a delegation record.
 * Validates: no self-delegation, no circular chains, no date overlap.
 * HR Admin approval required — approvedBy must be an HR_ADMIN person ID.
 */
export async function createDelegation(
  input: CreateDelegationInput
): Promise<WorkflowDelegation>
```

### 2.8 `switchHierarchyType` (Admin Escape Hatch)

```typescript
'use server'

/**
 * HR Admin can switch the hierarchy type for an in-flight workflow instance
 * in exceptional circumstances (e.g., wrong manager in org chart).
 * 
 * This re-resolves the current active step's approver using the new hierarchy type.
 * Audit event: HIERARCHY_SWITCHED with full rationale.
 * 
 * Restricted to: HR_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN
 */
export async function switchHierarchyType(input: {
  instanceId:       string
  newHierarchyType: HierarchyType
  newHierarchyLevel?: number
  newGroupId?:        string
  reason:           string
  authorizedBy:     string  // must be HR_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN
}): Promise<WorkflowInstanceV2>
```

### 2.9 `processSLABreaches` (Cron)

```typescript
/**
 * Called by cron job every 15 minutes.
 * NOT a server action — called from a background job runner.
 * 
 * Finds all active steps past their SLA deadline.
 * Applies per-step on_sla_breach action: ESCALATE / AUTO_APPROVE / AUTO_REJECT / NOTIFY_ONLY.
 */
export async function processSLABreaches(): Promise<SLABreachReport>
```

### 2.10 `resolveHierarchy` (Internal Service)

```typescript
/**
 * Pure hierarchy resolution service. NOT a server action.
 * Called internally by submitWorkflow and previewWorkflow.
 * 
 * Returns array of resolved approvers (parallel steps return multiple).
 * Includes full audit trail of vacancy handling and delegation.
 */
export async function resolveHierarchy(input: {
  hierarchyType:   HierarchyType
  hierarchyLevel?: number
  groupId?:        string
  role?:           string
  personId?:       string
  ruleId?:         string
  initiatorId:     string
  entityId:        string
  context:         WorkflowContext
  orgSnapshot:     HierarchySnapshot
  workflowDef:     WorkflowDefinitionV2
}): Promise<{
  approvers:           ResolvedApprover[]
  hierarchyPath:       string[]   // audit: which path was taken
  vacanciesEncountered: Array<{ positionId: string; resolution: string }>
  delegationsApplied:  Array<{ originalId: string; delegateId: string }>
}>
```

## 3. One-Click Email Approval Token Specification

### 3.1 Token Structure

Email notifications include signed action links for frictionless one-click approval.

```typescript
interface EmailActionToken {
  instanceStepId: string
  action:         'APPROVE' | 'REJECT'
  actorId:        string
  expiresAt:      number  // Unix timestamp = sla_deadline
  iat:            number  // issued at
  jti:            string  // unique token ID (prevents replay)
}
```

Signing algorithm: **HS256** using `process.env.WORKFLOW_TOKEN_SECRET`

### 3.2 Token Generation

```typescript
export function generateEmailActionToken(
  stepId:  string,
  action:  'APPROVE' | 'REJECT',
  actorId: string,
  slaDeadline: Date,
): string {
  const payload: EmailActionToken = {
    instanceStepId: stepId,
    action,
    actorId,
    expiresAt: Math.floor(slaDeadline.getTime() / 1000),
    iat: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    jti: crypto.randomUUID(),
  }
  return jwt.sign(payload, process.env.WORKFLOW_TOKEN_SECRET!, { algorithm: 'HS256' })
}
```

### 3.3 Token Validation Endpoint

**Route:** `GET/POST /api/workflow/action?token=<JWT>`

```typescript
// Handler logic:
export async function handleEmailAction(token: string): Promise<Response> {
  // 1. Verify JWT signature
  const payload = jwt.verify(token, process.env.WORKFLOW_TOKEN_SECRET!) as EmailActionToken
  
  // 2. Check expiry (JWT exp claim)
  if (Date.now() / 1000 > payload.expiresAt) {
    return redirect('/approvals/expired?reason=token_expired')
  }
  
  // 3. Check token has not been used (jti blacklist in Redis/DB)
  const used = await isTokenUsed(payload.jti)
  if (used) return redirect('/approvals/expired?reason=already_used')
  
  // 4. Mark token as used (atomic)
  await markTokenUsed(payload.jti, payload.expiresAt)
  
  // 5. Execute action — same as takeWorkflowAction
  const result = await takeWorkflowAction({
    instanceStepId: payload.instanceStepId,
    actorId:        payload.actorId,
    action:         payload.action,
  })
  
  // 6. Redirect to success page
  return redirect(`/approvals/${payload.instanceStepId}/confirmed?action=${payload.action}`)
}
```

**Security properties:**
- Single-use (jti tracked in `workflow_token_usage` table)
- Expires at SLA deadline (incentivizes timely action)
- Actor identity embedded (cannot be used by different approver)
- HTTPS-only (set `Secure` flag)

### 3.4 Email Template with Action Links

```
Subject: Action Required: Annual Leave Request — Aisha Khalidi (8 days)

Dear {{approver.name}},

{{employee.name}} has submitted an Annual Leave request requiring your approval.

Details:
  Employee:  {{employee.name}} ({{employee.number}})
  Department: {{employee.department}}
  Leave type: Annual Leave
  Duration:  {{request.days}} days
  Dates:     {{request.start_date}} → {{request.end_date}}
  Balance:   {{request.balance_remaining}} days remaining

You are Step {{step.order}} of {{total_steps}}: {{step.name}}
Approval deadline: {{sla_deadline}} ({{sla_hours_remaining}} working hours remaining)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                     │
│   [✓ APPROVE]              [✕ REJECT]               │
│                                                     │
│   approve_link              reject_link             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Or review full details: {{view_link}}

Note: These links expire at the approval deadline and can only be used once.

AVANIIS HR System
```
