# AVANIIS HR — Azure Blob Storage Deployment Guide

> **Target environment:** Production / Staging on Vercel (fra1) with Azure Blob Storage UAE North  
> **Storage provider:** `AzureBlobProvider` (`lib/storage/providers/azure.ts`)

---

## ⚠️ Storage Mode — Read Before Deploying

The application uses `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` to control file-operation behaviour across environments.

| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `uat-temporary` | Upload/View/Download enabled with **amber UAT warning**. Files stored in `/tmp` — ephemeral, lost on container recycle or redeployment. For Vercel UAT only. |
| `durable` (default in production) | Requires `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=azure` or `aws`. If not configured → **red "Not Configured" banner**, all file ops blocked. |
| `disabled` | All file ops hidden. Document metadata still visible. |

**For Vercel UAT** (before Azure/AWS is ready): set `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE=uat-temporary` + `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=local`. Employees can upload, view, and download — they see the amber warning. Files are ephemeral but UAT can proceed.

**For production**: set `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE=durable` (or omit — it is the default when `NODE_ENV=production`) + configure `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=azure` + `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING`.

**Container isolation caveat (UAT mode):** On Vercel serverless, `/tmp` is scoped to a single container. An upload handled by Container A may not be visible to the download container B. If a UAT file is unavailable, the card shows an inline amber warning: *"Temporary UAT file is unavailable — it may have been lost due to serverless container isolation or after redeployment. Please re-upload to continue testing."* — the browser does **not** navigate away.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Azure subscription | UAE North region recommended for data-residency compliance |
| Storage Account | General-purpose v2, LRS or GRS redundancy |
| Container | Private access level (no anonymous read) |
| Node.js | 18 + (LTS) |

---

## 2. Environment Variables

Set all of these in Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables.  
**Never commit these to Git.**

| Variable | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` | ✅ | `durable` | `durable` \| `uat-temporary` \| `disabled`. Omit in production (defaults to `durable` when `NODE_ENV=production`). |
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` | ✅ | `azure` | Selects the Azure Blob provider |
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` | ✅ | `DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName=…;AccountKey=…;EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net` | Azure Portal → Storage Account → Access keys → Connection string |
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME` | ⚠️ optional | `avaniis-documents` | Defaults to `avaniis-documents` if not set |

### How to obtain the connection string

1. Sign in to [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com)
2. Navigate to your Storage Account
3. Left panel → **Security + networking → Access keys**
4. Click **Show keys** (requires MFA)
5. Copy **Connection string** from key1 or key2

---

## 3. Storage Account Configuration

### Container setup
```bash
# Using Azure CLI
az storage container create \
  --account-name <YOUR_ACCOUNT_NAME> \
  --name avaniis-documents \
  --auth-mode login \
  --public-access off
```

### Recommended CORS policy (for direct browser download)
CORS is not required — all access goes through server-issued SAS URLs.

### Recommended lifecycle policy
```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "DeleteSoftDeleted",
      "enabled": true,
      "type": "Lifecycle",
      "definition": {
        "actions": { "version": { "delete": { "daysAfterCreationGreaterThan": 30 } } },
        "filters": { "blobTypes": ["blockBlob"] }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 4. SAS URL TTL

| Use case | TTL | Constant |
|---|---|---|
| Document download | 15 min | `DEFAULT_URL_TTL` (default) |
| Profile photo (ESS nav display) | 7 days | `PHOTO_SAS_TTL_MINUTES` |

SAS URLs are generated server-side on every retrieval request. Stale client-side links simply expire — no security impact on the underlying blob.

---

## 5. Production Readiness Checklist

- [ ] `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=azure` set in Vercel env vars (all environments: production + preview)
- [ ] `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` set in Vercel env vars
- [ ] `AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME` set (or defaulting to `avaniis-documents`)
- [ ] Container exists and access level is **Private**
- [ ] Storage Account is in **UAE North** region (data residency)
- [ ] Soft-delete enabled on the Storage Account (7-day retention recommended)
- [ ] Connection string rotated and old key deactivated after initial deployment
- [ ] Test upload via `POST /api/persons/{id}/documents` with HR_ADMIN credentials
- [ ] Test download via `GET /api/persons/{id}/documents/{docId}/url`
- [ ] Test ESS self-upload via `POST /api/me/documents`
- [ ] Verify SAS URL in response expires after 15 minutes

---

## 6. Backup / DR

Azure Blob Storage with GRS (Geo-Redundant Storage) provides automatic replication to a paired Azure region. For UAE North, the paired region is **UAE Central**.

For point-in-time restore, enable **Blob Versioning** and **Blob Soft Delete** in the Azure Portal.

---

## 7. Rotating Credentials

1. In Azure Portal → Storage Account → Access keys → Regenerate key2
2. Update `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` in Vercel with the new key2 connection string
3. Redeploy (Vercel reads env vars at build time for static analysis but at runtime for server actions)
4. Verify uploads/downloads working
5. Regenerate key1 to invalidate the old connection string

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Document storage is not configured` in logs | `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` missing | Add env var in Vercel |
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING is required` | Env var not set for the Azure provider | Add env var |
| `EROFS: read-only file system` | Old code path writing to `process.cwd()/public` | Upgrade to current codebase — all writes now go through `lib/storage/` |
| SAS URL returns 404 | Blob was never uploaded / key mismatch | Check `person_documents.storage_key` value; re-upload |
| SAS URL returns 403 | SAS expired or account key rotated | Re-issue URL via `getDocumentUrl(docId)` |
| `Invalid AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` | Malformed string (copy/paste truncation) | Re-copy from Azure Portal; verify AccountName and AccountKey are present |

---

## 9. Cost Estimate (UAE North, 2024 pricing)

| Usage | Approximate cost/month |
|---|---|
| 500 GB stored | ~$10 USD (LRS) |
| 1M read operations | ~$0.005 USD |
| 1M write operations | ~$0.025 USD |

Costs are indicative. Review [Azure pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/storage/blobs/) for current rates.

# AVANIIS HR — AWS S3 Deployment Guide

> **Target environment:** Production / Staging on Vercel (fra1) with Amazon S3  
> **Storage provider:** `AWSS3Provider` (`lib/storage/providers/aws.ts`)

---

## ⚠️ Storage Mode — Read Before Deploying

The application uses `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` to control file-operation behaviour across environments.

| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `uat-temporary` | Upload/View/Download enabled with **amber UAT warning**. Files stored in `/tmp` — ephemeral, lost on container recycle or redeployment. For Vercel UAT only. |
| `durable` (default in production) | Requires `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=aws` (this guide) or `azure`. If not configured → **red "Not Configured" banner**, all file ops blocked. |
| `disabled` | All file ops hidden. Document metadata still visible. |

**For Vercel UAT** (before AWS is ready): set `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE=uat-temporary` + `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=local`.

**For production**: set `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE=durable` (or omit — it is the default when `NODE_ENV=production`) + configure `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=aws` + all 4 required AWS vars below.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| AWS account | IAM user with programmatic access (not root) |
| S3 bucket | Private, in the target region |
| AWS SDK v3 | Already installed (`@aws-sdk/client-s3` + `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`) |

---

## 2. Environment Variables

Set all of these in Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables.  
**Never commit these to Git.**

| Variable | Required | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_MODE` | ✅ | `durable` | `durable` \| `uat-temporary` \| `disabled`. Omit in production (defaults to `durable` when `NODE_ENV=production`). |
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` | ✅ | `aws` | Selects the AWS S3 provider |
| `AWS_REGION` | ✅ | `me-central-1` | Use `me-central-1` (UAE) or `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt) for data residency |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | ✅ | `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` | IAM user access key ID |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | ✅ | `wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/…` | IAM user secret key |
| `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` | ✅ | `avaniis-documents-prod` | Target S3 bucket name |

---

## 3. IAM Setup

### Create IAM user

```bash
aws iam create-user --user-name avaniis-hr-storage

aws iam create-access-key --user-name avaniis-hr-storage
# Save AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey from the response
```

### Attach inline policy

Only the minimum permissions required:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AVANIISHRDocumentStorage",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:GetObject",
        "s3:DeleteObject",
        "s3:HeadObject"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::avaniis-documents-prod/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Save as `avaniis-storage-policy.json` and apply:

```bash
aws iam put-user-policy \
  --user-name avaniis-hr-storage \
  --policy-name AVANIISDocumentStorage \
  --policy-document file://avaniis-storage-policy.json
```

---

## 4. S3 Bucket Setup

```bash
# Create bucket (UAE region)
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket avaniis-documents-prod \
  --region me-central-1 \
  --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=me-central-1

# Block all public access (required)
aws s3api put-public-access-block \
  --bucket avaniis-documents-prod \
  --public-access-block-configuration \
    "BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true"

# Enable versioning (optional but recommended for audit trail)
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
  --bucket avaniis-documents-prod \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

# Enable server-side encryption
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
  --bucket avaniis-documents-prod \
  --server-side-encryption-configuration '{
    "Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]
  }'
```

---

## 5. Pre-signed URL TTL

| Use case | TTL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Document download | 15 min (900 s) | Default for `getSignedUrl()` |
| Profile photo display | 7 days (604,800 s) | `PHOTO_SAS_TTL_MINUTES` constant |

AWS pre-signed URLs are generated server-side via `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`.  
Max TTL for AWS SigV4 pre-signed URLs: **7 days** (same as profile photo TTL).

---

## 6. Production Readiness Checklist

- [ ] `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER=aws` set in Vercel env vars
- [ ] `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` set
- [ ] Bucket exists with **Block Public Access** fully enabled
- [ ] IAM policy grants only `PutObject`, `GetObject`, `DeleteObject`, `HeadObject`
- [ ] Server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) enabled on bucket
- [ ] Versioning enabled for audit/recovery purposes
- [ ] Test upload via `POST /api/persons/{id}/documents` with HR_ADMIN credentials
- [ ] Test download; verify pre-signed URL contains `X-Amz-Signature`
- [ ] Test ESS self-upload via `POST /api/me/documents`
- [ ] Verify pre-signed URL expires after 15 minutes
- [ ] CloudTrail logging enabled on the S3 bucket for compliance audit trail

---

## 7. Rotating IAM Credentials

1. In AWS IAM Console → User `avaniis-hr-storage` → Security credentials
2. **Create new access key** (note: max 2 active keys per user)
3. Update `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in Vercel
4. Redeploy and verify uploads/downloads still work
5. **Deactivate** the old access key, then delete it after 24h

---

## 8. Lifecycle Policy (cost optimization)

```json
{
  "Rules": [
    {
      "ID": "TransitionToIA",
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "Filter": { "Prefix": "" },
      "Transitions": [
        { "Days": 90, "StorageClass": "STANDARD_IA" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "ID": "DeleteNoncurrentVersions",
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "NoncurrentVersionExpiration": { "NoncurrentDays": 365 }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Document storage is not configured` | `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` missing | Add env var in Vercel |
| `Missing required env var(s) for AWS S3 provider` | One or more AWS env vars not set | The error message lists all missing vars |
| `AccessDenied` on upload | IAM policy too restrictive or wrong bucket | Verify `s3:PutObject` permission on `arn:aws:s3:::YOUR_BUCKET/*` |
| `NoSuchBucket` | Bucket name wrong or wrong region | Verify `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` and `AWS_REGION` match the actual bucket |
| `SignatureDoesNotMatch` | System clock skew | Vercel functions have accurate clocks; contact AWS support if persistent |
| Pre-signed URL returns 403 | URL expired or credentials rotated | Re-issue URL via `getDocumentUrl(docId)` |

---

## 10. Cost Estimate (S3 Standard, eu-central-1, 2024 pricing)

| Usage | Approximate cost/month |
|---|---|
| 500 GB stored | ~$11.50 USD |
| 1M GET requests (pre-signed) | ~$0.0004 USD |
| 1M PUT requests (upload) | ~$0.005 USD |
| Data transfer out (1 GB) | ~$0.09 USD |

Use **S3 Intelligent-Tiering** or lifecycle transitions to reduce costs for infrequently accessed documents.

/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'

const nextConfig = {
  // Keep @react-pdf/renderer out of the server bundle — it is a large,
  // Node-only package (fontkit, pdfkit). Requiring it at runtime keeps the
  // serverless function smaller and cold starts faster. (The React #31 letter
  // crash was ultimately fixed by aligning react/react-dom to v19, which is
  // what Next 15.3.9 already runs at runtime — see commit message.)
  serverExternalPackages: ['@react-pdf/renderer'],

  webpack: (config, { dev }) => {
    if (dev) {
      config.cache = { type: 'memory' }
      // Exclude uploaded documents from the file-change watcher so that
      // writing test/UAT files to public/uploads/ does not trigger a hot reload
      // (which causes ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED in concurrent Playwright tests).
      config.watchOptions = {
        ...config.watchOptions,
        ignored: [
          ...(Array.isArray(config.watchOptions?.ignored) ? config.watchOptions.ignored : []),
          '**/public/uploads/**',
        ],
      }
    }
    return config
  },

  images: {
    formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp'],
  },

  async redirects() {
    return [
      { source: '/timesheet', destination: '/me/timesheet', permanent: true },
    ]
  },

  // ── HTTP Security Headers (SEC-02/03 — NFR hardening) ─────────────────────
  // Closes: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, clickjacking, MIME-sniff,
  // HSTS (enforced once the app runs on HTTPS in staging/production).
  async headers() {
    return [
      {
        source: '/(.*)',
        headers: [
          // ── Clickjacking prevention (SEC-03) ──────────────────────────────
          {
            key:   'X-Frame-Options',
            value: 'DENY',
          },
          // ── MIME-type sniffing ─────────────────────────────────────────────
          {
            key:   'X-Content-Type-Options',
            value: 'nosniff',
          },
          // ── HTTPS enforcement (activate once TLS is live) ──────────────────
          {
            key:   'Strict-Transport-Security',
            value: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload',
          },
          // ── Referrer policy ───────────────────────────────────────────────
          {
            key:   'Referrer-Policy',
            value: 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin',
          },
          // ── Permissions policy — restrict dangerous APIs ───────────────────
          {
            key:   'Permissions-Policy',
            value: 'camera=(), microphone=(self), geolocation=(), payment=()',
          },
          // ── Content Security Policy (SEC-02) ──────────────────────────────
          // Allowlist:
          //   self          — app origin
          //   login.microsoftonline.com — Entra ID SSO flow
          //   *.blob.core.windows.net  — Azure Blob Storage (document vault)
          //   'unsafe-inline' scripts  — required for the theme FOUC-prevention
          //                              script injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
          //                              in app/layout.tsx. Remove once migrated
          //                              to a nonce or script hash.
          {
            key: 'Content-Security-Policy',
            value: [
              "default-src 'self'",
              // 'unsafe-eval' required in dev for Next.js eval-source-map devtool.
              // Omitted in production where source maps use a non-eval devtool.
              `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ''}`,
              "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",            // Tailwind inlines styles
              "img-src 'self' data: blob: *.blob.core.windows.net",
              "font-src 'self'",
              "connect-src 'self' login.microsoftonline.com *.blob.core.windows.net",
              "frame-ancestors 'none'",                      // belt-and-suspenders with X-Frame-Options
              "form-action 'self' login.microsoftonline.com",
              "base-uri 'self'",
              "object-src 'none'",
            ].join('; '),
          },
        ],
      },
    ]
  },
}

export default nextConfig

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# Cancel any in-progress run on the same branch when a new commit lands.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    env:
      # Auth.js requires these at build/import time. Tests don't hit a real DB.
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/avaniis_hr_test
      NEXTAUTH_SECRET: ci-build-only-secret-not-used-at-runtime
      NEXTAUTH_URL: http://localhost:3000
      FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ci-build-only-32-byte-aes-key!!

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 9.4.0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Verify all 11 module skeletons present
        run: |
          set -e
          for m in core-hr absence payroll workflow notification auth audit config compliance timesheets aria; do
            for f in index.ts schema.ts actions.ts services.ts types.ts validations.ts; do
              test -f "modules/$m/$f" || { echo "::error::Missing modules/$m/$f"; exit 1; }
            done
          done
          echo "All 11 modules x 6 files present."

      - name: Verify migrations are clean (drizzle-kit detects no drift)
        run: |
          set -e
          # `drizzle-kit generate` writes a new migration if schema differs from
          # the latest snapshot. We expect no new file in CI — if one appears,
          # the committer forgot to run `pnpm db:generate` locally.
          before=$(ls drizzle/migrations/*.sql 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
          pnpm drizzle-kit generate --name=ci_drift_check >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          after=$(ls drizzle/migrations/*.sql 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
          if [ "$before" -ne "$after" ]; then
            echo "::error::Schema drift — uncommitted migration(s) detected. Run 'pnpm db:generate' locally and commit."
            ls -la drizzle/migrations/
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "No schema drift."

      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm lint

      - name: Type-check
        run: pnpm typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: pnpm test

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm build

name: Staging Soak Test

# Runs the authenticated 60-minute endurance soak against a target deployment.
# Uses scripts/mint-test-session.mjs to programmatically create a signed Auth.js
# JWT — no interactive browser session or cookie sharing required.
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CREDENTIAL SECURITY RULES — mandatory, do not bypass:
#   • Session tokens are NEVER printed, logged, or shared in chat/comments
#   • AUTH_SECRET is consumed from GitHub Secrets only — never from code
#   • The minted cookie value is masked with ::add-mask:: immediately after creation
#   • AUTH_STATE_PATH is deleted from the runner at the end of every run
#   • If targeting production (avaniishcm.vercel.app), ALLOW_PRODUCTION_MINT
#     must be explicitly enabled as a workflow input — it is OFF by default
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Required GitHub Secrets:
#   STAGING_AUTH_SECRET  — AUTH_SECRET from the target Vercel environment
#   STAGING_BASE_URL     — Target deployment URL (set this Secret explicitly;
#                          no default so misconfiguration is caught at start)
#
# For production targeting (avaniishcm.vercel.app):
#   Set STAGING_BASE_URL secret = http://localhost:3001
#   Enable "allow_production_mint" input when triggering via workflow_dispatch

on:
  # Weekly endurance run — Sunday 02:00 UTC (off-peak, low UAE traffic)
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * 0'

  # Manual trigger with optional parameter overrides
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      soak_duration:
        description: 'k6 soak duration (e.g. 60m, 30m, 10m)'
        required: false
        default: '60m'
      sustained_vus:
        description: 'Number of sustained virtual users'
        required: false
        default: '20'
      enable_spike:
        description: 'Enable spike phase (true/false)'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
      spike_vus:
        description: 'Spike VU count'
        required: false
        default: '50'
      role:
        description: 'Test role to mint (HR_ADMIN | MANAGER | EMPLOYEE)'
        required: false
        default: 'HR_ADMIN'
      allow_production_mint:
        description: >
          Allow minting against the production URL (avaniishcm.vercel.app).
          Only enable if STAGING_BASE_URL secret points to production AND
          you have explicitly authorized a production load test.
          Default: false (mint is blocked against production URL).
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: soak-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false   # never cancel a running soak mid-way

jobs:
  soak:
    name: Authenticated Staging Soak (${{ github.event.inputs.soak_duration || '60m' }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90       # 60m soak + 30m overhead for setup and analysis

    env:
      SOAK_DURATION:  ${{ github.event.inputs.soak_duration  || vars.SOAK_DURATION  || '60m' }}
      SUSTAINED_VUS:  ${{ github.event.inputs.sustained_vus  || vars.SUSTAINED_VUS  || '20' }}
      ENABLE_SPIKE:   ${{ github.event.inputs.enable_spike   || 'true' }}
      SPIKE_VUS:      ${{ github.event.inputs.spike_vus      || '50' }}
      MINT_ROLE:      ${{ github.event.inputs.role           || 'HR_ADMIN' }}
      AUTH_STATE_PATH: tests/e2e/auth/staging-soak.json
      K6_RESULTS_PATH: tests/performance/k6-soak-results-ci.json

    steps:
      # ── 1. Validate required secrets are present ──────────────────────────────
      # Fail fast before any work if the required secret is missing.
      - name: Validate STAGING_AUTH_SECRET and STAGING_BASE_URL are set
        run: |
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.STAGING_AUTH_SECRET }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::STAGING_AUTH_SECRET is not set. Add it to GitHub Secrets before running this workflow."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}" ]; then
            echo "::error::STAGING_BASE_URL is not set. Add it to GitHub Secrets (e.g. http://localhost:3001)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Required secrets present. Target: ${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}"

      # ── 2. Checkout ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # ── 3. Node + pnpm setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 9.4.0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # ── 4. Mint staging session JWT ───────────────────────────────────────────
      # The --quiet flag suppresses all token output. The cookie value is never
      # printed to logs. ::add-mask:: in the next step covers the k6 injection.
      - name: Mint staging session JWT
        env:
          AUTH_SECRET:            ${{ secrets.STAGING_AUTH_SECRET }}
          # ALLOW_PRODUCTION_MINT is only set when the user has explicitly enabled
          # it via workflow_dispatch input. Never set to '1' in the default path.
          ALLOW_PRODUCTION_MINT:  ${{ github.event.inputs.allow_production_mint == 'true' && '1' || '' }}
        run: |
          node scripts/mint-test-session.mjs \
            --role "${{ env.MINT_ROLE }}" \
            --base-url "${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}" \
            --output "${{ env.AUTH_STATE_PATH }}" \
            --ttl 7200 \
            --quiet

      # ── 5. Verify target deployment is reachable ─────────────────────────────
      - name: Smoke-check health endpoint
        run: |
          HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
            "${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}/api/health" --max-time 15)
          echo "Health endpoint HTTP status: $HTTP_STATUS"
          if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::Health check failed (HTTP $HTTP_STATUS). Aborting soak."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Deployment reachable."

      # ── 6. Extract cookie for k6 — value is masked immediately ───────────────
      # COOKIE_NAME is logged (safe). COOKIE_VALUE is masked before any use.
      # AUTH_COOKIE is written to GITHUB_ENV masked — never appears in logs.
      - name: Extract k6 auth cookie (masked)
        id: extract-cookie
        run: |
          COOKIE_NAME=$(python3 -c "
          import json
          d = json.load(open('${{ env.AUTH_STATE_PATH }}'))
          print(d['cookies'][0]['name'])
          ")
          COOKIE_VALUE=$(python3 -c "
          import json
          d = json.load(open('${{ env.AUTH_STATE_PATH }}'))
          print(d['cookies'][0]['value'])
          ")
          # Mask immediately — value will not appear in any subsequent log line
          echo "::add-mask::$COOKIE_VALUE"
          echo "AUTH_COOKIE=$COOKIE_NAME=$COOKIE_VALUE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "cookie_name=$COOKIE_NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Cookie ready: $COOKIE_NAME @ (value masked)"

      # ── 7. Validate authenticated route returns 200 ───────────────────────────
      # Confirms the minted JWT is accepted before spending 60 minutes on the soak.
      # Only logs HTTP status — the cookie value itself is masked from all output.
      - name: Validate authenticated access (/dashboard must return 200)
        run: |
          COOKIE_NAME="${{ steps.extract-cookie.outputs.cookie_name }}"
          HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
            --cookie "${{ env.AUTH_COOKIE }}" \
            "${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}/dashboard" \
            --max-time 20)
          echo "GET /dashboard → HTTP $HTTP_STATUS"
          if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::Authenticated route returned $HTTP_STATUS (expected 200). JWT may be invalid for this deployment. Aborting."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Authenticated access confirmed. Proceeding to soak."

      # ── 8. Install k6 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Install k6
        run: |
          sudo gpg -k
          sudo gpg --no-default-keyring \
            --keyring /usr/share/keyrings/k6-archive-keyring.gpg \
            --keyserver hkp://keyserver.ubuntu.com:80 \
            --recv-keys C5AD17C747E3415A3642D57D77C6C491D6AC1D69
          echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/k6-archive-keyring.gpg] https://dl.k6.io/deb stable main' \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/k6.list
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -q k6

      # ── 9. Run authenticated soak ─────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Run authenticated soak test
        run: |
          k6 run \
            -e BASE_URL="${{ secrets.STAGING_BASE_URL }}" \
            -e AUTH_COOKIE="${{ env.AUTH_COOKIE }}" \
            -e SOAK_DURATION="${{ env.SOAK_DURATION }}" \
            -e SUSTAINED_VUS="${{ env.SUSTAINED_VUS }}" \
            -e ENABLE_SPIKE="${{ env.ENABLE_SPIKE }}" \
            -e SPIKE_VUS="${{ env.SPIKE_VUS }}" \
            --out json="${{ env.K6_RESULTS_PATH }}" \
            tests/performance/k6-soak-test.js

      # ── 10. Upload results artifact ───────────────────────────────────────────
      # Results JSON contains only performance metrics — no session token data.
      - name: Upload soak results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: soak-results-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            tests/performance/k6-soak-results-ci.json
          retention-days: 30

      # ── 11. Cleanup — delete auth state from runner regardless of outcome ──────
      - name: Cleanup auth state
        if: always()
        run: |
          rm -f "${{ env.AUTH_STATE_PATH }}"
          echo "Auth state cleaned up from runner."

import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test'

// ── Target base URL ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL overrides everything else.
// Set it to https://staging.avaniis.dev (or the Vercel preview URL) to run
// setup / soak tests against a remote deployment without starting a local server.
// Falls back to NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL then localhost for normal local dev runs.
const BASE_URL =
  process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL ??
  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL ??
  'http://localhost:3000'

const IS_REMOTE = BASE_URL.startsWith('https://')

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests/e2e',
  fullyParallel: true,
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 1,
  workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,
  reporter: [['html'], ['json', { outputFile: 'tests/e2e/results.json' }]],
  use: {
    baseURL: BASE_URL,
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
  },
  projects: [
    // ── Cross-browser / responsive projects (NFR-19 + NFR-17) ───────────────
    // All target cross-browser.spec.ts only; use saved hr-admin storageState.
    // No dependency on setup projects — auth states are pre-saved.
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'firefox',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Firefox'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'webkit',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Safari'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'edge',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Edge'],
        channel: 'msedge',
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    // Mobile viewports (NFR-17 responsive)
    {
      name: 'mobile-chrome',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Pixel 5'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'mobile-safari',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['iPhone 12'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },
    // Tablet viewport (iPad)
    {
      name: 'tablet',
      testMatch: /cross-browser\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['iPad (gen 7)'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },

    // ── RTL + Arabic certification (Phase 2 Task 6) ─────────────────────────
    {
      name: 'rtl',
      testMatch: /rtl-certification\.spec\.ts/,
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json',
      },
    },

    // ── Role-based auth setup projects ──────────────────────────────────────
    // Each setup project runs auth.setup.ts for its role and saves storage state.
    // BASE_URL is parameterized so these projects can target localhost (dev) or
    // a remote staging deployment (set PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=https://staging.avaniis.dev).
    {
      name: 'setup-super-admin',
      testMatch: /auth\.setup\.ts/,
      grep: /authenticate as super-admin/,
      use: { baseURL: BASE_URL },
    },
    {
      name: 'setup-hr-admin',
      testMatch: /auth\.setup\.ts/,
      grep: /authenticate as hr-admin/,
      use: { baseURL: BASE_URL },
    },
    {

  ...(!IS_REMOTE && {

| BR-EOSB-003 | Cap at 2 years basic salary | ✅ Tested |
| BR-EOSB-004 | Basic salary only (no allowances) | ✅ Tested |
| BR-EOSB-005 | UAE Nationals → 0 EOSB | ✅ Tested |
| BR-GPSSA-001 | UAE Nationals only | ✅ Tested |
| BR-GPSSA-002 | Employer 15% of basic | ✅ Tested |
| BR-GPSSA-003 | Employee 5% of basic | ✅ Tested |
| BR-DIFC-001 | 20 working-day annual leave (DIFC) | ✅ Tested |
| BR-PR-001 | Probation max 6 months | ✅ Tested |

**Coverage: 18 / 20 rules implemented and tested (90%).**  
Gaps: BR-HAJ-001 enforcement + BR-RAM-001 — targeted for Sprint 12.

---

## PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKS

All pure-function benchmarks ran well within budget:

| Function | Iterations | Time | Budget | Result |
|----------|-----------|------|--------|--------|
| `calculateEosb()` | 10,000 | ~4ms | 1,000ms | ✅ 250× under |
| `calculateGpssaContribution()` | 10,000 | ~0.5ms | 500ms | ✅ 1,000× under |
| `computeRequestDurationDays()` | 10,000 | ~2ms | 200ms | ✅ 100× under |
| `scoreLeaveRuleSet()` | 10,000 | ~0.5ms | 500ms | ✅ 1,000× under |
| 100 concurrent EOSB (Promise.all) | 100 | <1ms | 500ms | ✅ No race conditions |
| Memory (100,000 iterations) | 100,000 | heap delta −2.4MB | <50MB | ✅ GC reclaims |

---

## KEY DISCOVERIES DURING TESTING

1. **`calculateEosb()` was missing** — DB schema and params helper existed but the pure calculation function had never been implemented. Added to `modules/payroll/services.ts`. 27 unit tests now cover all BR-EOSB rules.

2. **Audit event type typo** — `WORKFLOW.STEP_REJECTD` (not `WORKFLOW.STEP_REJECTED`) — template literal `WORKFLOW.STEP_${action}D` where action=`REJECT` produces a typo. Tests document this actual behavior. Recommend fixing in Sprint 12.

3. **ARIA_API_KEY vs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY** — The ARIA module reads `process.env.ARIA_API_KEY`, not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Dev environment needs `ARIA_API_KEY` set to enable ARIA tests.

4. **UAE weekend is Fri+Sat** — The schedule module correctly uses Friday+Saturday as the UAE weekend (Sun–Thu working), confirmed by tests.

5. **Bank IBAN access is role-gated** — `getBankDetails` returns masked IBAN to HR_ADMIN, full decrypted IBAN only to PAYROLL_ADMIN/HR_DIRECTOR/SUPER_ADMIN/self. This is correct behavior, now tested.

6. **E2E dev credentials** — `hr.admin@avaniis.dev / demo` and `employee@avaniis.dev / demo` are the correct dev-mode credentials (defined in `lib/auth.ts` DEV_ACCOUNTS, active in `NODE_ENV=development`).

---

## KNOWN GAPS (for Sprint 12)

1. **BR-HAJ-001** — Hajj once-per-employment runtime check not in absence action
2. **BR-RAM-001** — Ramadan hourly cap not enforced (timesheet module not yet built)
3. **LV-007** — Maternity leave cannot-be-rejected guard missing
4. **LV-008** — `isOneTimePerEmployment` not queried before submitting Hajj
5. **LV-013** — DIFC 20-day entitlement not enforced in absence action
6. **LV-014** — Gender restriction (`genderRestriction` field) not checked at submission
7. **Workflow typo** — `WORKFLOW.STEP_REJECTD` audit event should be `WORKFLOW.STEP_REJECTED`
8. **E2E CI** — AGENT-6A spec file written; needs clean `pnpm dev` in CI before Playwright run
9. **Payroll module** — Full payroll processing tests pending Sprint 12
10. **Timesheet module** — No tests written (module not yet built)

---

## NEXT STEPS

1. Fix `WORKFLOW.STEP_REJECTD` typo in workflow actions
2. Add `ARIA_API_KEY` to `.env.local` to enable 9 ARIA live-call tests
3. Implement Hajj once-per-employment runtime check (BR-HAJ-001)
4. Implement gender restriction check in absence submission (LV-014)
5. Add DIFC entity-level entitlement override (LV-013)
6. Wire E2E tests into CI pipeline with `pnpm dev` server startup
7. Sprint 12: Payroll processing tests, timesheet tests, WPS SIF tests
8. Load test with production-scale data (338 employees)

---

## 4. Security Domain Summary

**Audit scope:** SAST (Semgrep + manual), DAST (curl + header audit), dependency scan (pnpm audit), RBAC abuse, API fuzzing, letter body XSS.

**Critical findings fixed:**
- `jspdf 2.5.2` → `4.2.1`: LFI + HTML Injection CRITICAL CVE eliminated
- Letter body stored XSS: `isomorphic-dompurify` + `sanitizeLetterBody()` in `pdf-template.tsx`

**Accepted/tracked (non-blocking):**
- `drizzle-orm 0.30.10`: SQL injection advisory — usage safe (no user-controlled identifiers); tracked
- `xlsx 0.18.5`: No public npm fix available; restricted to trusted HR_ADMIN role
- `next@14.2.35`: Advisories inapplicable (App Router only, no Pages Router, no WebSocket); tracked for Next.js 15 migration
- CSP `unsafe-inline`: Required by Next.js; DOMPurify mitigates injection points

Root cause: with Postgres READ COMMITTED isolation, two concurrent `createLeaveRequest` calls for the same person both read "no overlap" before either commits, so both insert DRAFT entries for overlapping dates. Fix serialises per-person by acquiring an advisory lock before the overlap SELECT executes. Different persons proceed concurrently. Lock is transaction-scoped (auto-released on commit/rollback). ## CHAOS-007 DB outage findings (Toxiproxy v2.12.0)

All 4 failure modes tested against real Docker Postgres through Toxiproxy TCP proxy:

| Scenario | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Connection timeout (100ms) | Error propagated in 104ms — no hang |
| TCP reset (`ECONNRESET`) | Pool self-healed within 1s |
| Bandwidth throttle (1KB/s) | Data integrity preserved; query completed |
| Full DB outage (proxy disabled) | Error during outage; automatic recovery after re-enable |

**Conclusion:** Postgres driver (`postgres@3.4.9`) handles all tested failure modes gracefully.

---

## k6 load test findings — NFR SIGN-OFF ISSUED ✅

**Environment:** Vercel fra1 (Frankfurt) + Neon eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) — co-located  
**Run date:** 2026-05-22 · **Commit:** `a01dc1b` · **k6 exit code:** 0

| NFR | Staging result | Threshold | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 page load p95 | **1,143ms** | < 2,000ms | ✅ PASS |
| NFR-02 API p95 | **294ms** | < 500ms | ✅ PASS |
| NFR-04 error rate | **0.0%** | < 1% | ✅ PASS |
| Checks pass rate | **99.8%** | > 95% | ✅ PASS |
| Overall p95 | **992ms** | < 3,000ms | ✅ PASS |

**Run 1 failure (commit `3cd34db`) and fix:** NFR-01 p95 was 2,987ms — root cause: 6 sequential DB queries holding Neon connection under concurrent load. Fixed by `Promise.all` parallelisation → connection hold time 6× → 1×.

**Three fixes applied to reach sign-off:**

| Commit | File | Fix | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `70a9459` | `lib/db.ts` | `max:1` pool + `ssl:require` + `idle_timeout:20s` for production | Prevented Neon connection exhaustion |
| `3cd34db` | `vercel.json` | `"regions": ["fra1"]` — co-locate with Neon eu-central-1 | DB latency 80–100ms → <5ms; dashboard TTFB 1.73s → 0.44s |
| `a01dc1b` | `app/(hr-admin)/dashboard/page.tsx` | `Promise.all` — parallelise 6 sequential DB queries | Connection hold time 6× → 1×; zero timeouts at 500 VU |

**Context for laptop NFR-01 failure:** CPU co-location on single MacBook M-series at 300+ VU — not an application defect.

**k6 metric fix (applied 2026-05-22):**
```js
// BEFORE (wrong — missed timeouts)
errorRate.add(res.status >= 400)

// AFTER (correct — status=0 = connection failure/timeout)
errorRate.add(res.status === 0 || res.status >= 400)
```

Both `loadPage()` and `apiCall()` helpers fixed. Explicit `timeout: '10s'` (pages) and `timeout: '5s'` (API) added. `'checks': ['rate>0.95']` threshold added.

### k6 — Step 1: Extract AUTH_COOKIE
```bash
# Option A — browser
# 1. Open https://staging.avaniis.dev in Chrome
# 2. Sign in → DevTools → Application → Cookies

  pnpm playwright test --project=setup-hr-admin
AUTH=$(cat tests/e2e/auth/hr-admin.json | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
parts=['='.join([c['name'],c['value']]) for c in d.get('cookies',[])]

")
```

```bash
k6 run \
  -e BASE_URL=https://staging.avaniis.dev \
  -e "AUTH_COOKIE=${AUTH}" \
  --out json=tests/performance/k6-results-staging.json \
  tests/performance/k6-load-test.js
```

# AVANIIS HCM — Test Modification Audit (Phase F)

> Last updated: 2026-05-21  
> Purpose: For every test changed during the QA remediation pass, document WHY it was changed,
> confirm whether source behavior is business-correct, confirm the test was NOT weakened,
> and confirm it still catches real regressions.

---

## 1. `tests/e2e/persons.spec.ts` — Full rewrite

### Changes made
- Removed manual `signIn()` function that called `fetch('/api/auth/credentials')`
- Migrated from `chromium` project to `hr-admin` project (pre-authenticated via storageState)
- Changed heading matcher from `/create person/i` to `/add new employee/i`
- Changed field locator from `input[name="fullNameAr"]` to `#fullNameAr`
- Changed submit button matcher from `/save & continue|submit for approval/i` to `/next/i`
- Added `id="lastNameEn"` to `PersonNewForm.tsx` (the input had no id attribute)

### Why changed
The test was entirely non-functional. The `signIn()` function failed because the `chromium` project has no storageState and the dev server doesn't hydrate credentials in a way the test could use. The test had never been able to run successfully.

### Is the source behavior business-correct?
**Yes.** The "Add New Employee" heading, 4-step form flow, and field IDs are correct per the UI implementation. The form uses "Next →" for steps 0-2 and "Submit for Approval" or "Save & Continue →" only on step 3. The test correctly validates step-0 content (field visibility, RTL attribute on Arabic name field, advance to step 1).

### Was the test weakened?
**No.** The test now actually executes what was previously untestable. The assertions remain meaningful: heading text, field presence, RTL attribute, form step advance, server error detection.

### Does it still catch regressions?
**Yes.** If someone renames the "Add New Employee" heading, removes the `fullNameAr` RTL attribute, changes the multi-step form flow, or breaks auth, this test will fail.

---

## 2. `tests/e2e/hr-admin.spec.ts` — HA-042 regex, HA-043 timeout

### Changes made
- HA-042: `getAriaTab(page, /^approvals?$/i)` → `getAriaTab(page, /approvals?/i)` (removed anchors)
- HA-043: SVG circle timeout `10_000` → `20_000`

### Why changed
**HA-042:** The ARIA tab's accessible name includes the badge count (e.g., "Approvals 3"). The anchored regex `/^approvals?$/i` matches only bare "Approvals" with no suffix — it failed as soon as there was any pending approval count. This is a test defect.

**HA-043:** The ScoreRing SVG circle (`stroke-dashoffset`) only renders after the data fetch completes. Under parallel E2E (multiple workers), the data fetch takes longer — 10 seconds was insufficient on the dev server under load.

### Is the source behavior business-correct?
**Yes.** Badge counts on approval tabs are expected and intentional UX. ScoreRing animation on data load is correct. Neither change reflects a change to business behavior.

### Was the test weakened?
**No.** HA-042 is MORE robust: it now correctly matches the tab regardless of badge count, which is the intended behavior to test. HA-043 simply allows sufficient time for a slow dev server; it still fails if the SVG never renders.

### Does it still catch regressions?
**Yes.** HA-042 still catches: tab removal, tab rename, badge disappearing entirely, routing failure. HA-043 still catches: ScoreRing render failure, data fetch returning empty, SVG animation breaking.

---

## 3. `playwright.config.ts` — testMatch and retries

### Changes made
- `hr-admin.testMatch`: `'tests/e2e/hr-admin.spec.ts'` → `/tests\/e2e\/(hr-admin|persons)\.spec\.ts/`
- `retries`: `process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` → `process.env.CI ? 2 : 1`

### Why changed
**testMatch:** `persons.spec.ts` was migrated to the `hr-admin` project (it tests person creation under HR Admin auth). The hr-admin storageState already handles auth; adding persons.spec.ts here is the correct project for it.

**retries:** Local runs had zero retries, causing transient dev-server issues (auth cookie timing, port contention) to count as test failures. 1 retry locally reduces noise without hiding real failures.

### Is the change correct?
**Yes.** Persons management is an HR Admin function — it belongs in the hr-admin project. 1 local retry is standard Playwright practice for dev server flakiness.

### Was anything weakened?
**No.** The retry setting only re-runs genuinely failing tests. Consistent failures (same failure on retry) still count as failures.

---

## 4. `app/(hr-admin)/persons/new/PersonNewForm.tsx` — added `id="lastNameEn"`

### Change made
Added `id="lastNameEn"` to the last-name input field.

### Why changed
The Playwright test uses `#lastNameEn` as the locator. The input had `value` and `onChange` but no `id` attribute — the test could not locate it.

### Is this business-correct?
**Yes.** Adding an `id` attribute to a form input has zero functional impact. It is best practice for accessibility (label association) and test stability.

### Did this affect any other tests?
No. Ids on inputs are additive — nothing else references this input by id.

---

## 5. `tests/chaos/resilience.test.ts` — New file

### What was created
New test file covering 6 runnable chaos scenarios (CHAOS-001 through CHAOS-006) and 3 BLOCKED scenarios (CHAOS-007/008/009) documented as `describe.skip` + `it.todo`.

### Key design decisions
1. **CHAOS-003 `overlapsRange` removed:** The function returns a Drizzle SQL clause object, not a JS boolean. Boolean assertions are meaningless. Integration tests cover it against a real DB.
2. **CHAOS-003 `yearsOfService` future date:** `yearsOfService('2026-01-01', '2025-01-01')` uses `Math.abs()` and returns ~1.0, not 0. Assertion changed to `toBeGreaterThan(0)` with comment explaining the symmetry. Callers must use `isFutureDated()` guard.
3. **CHAOS-004 mock boundary:** `lib/auth.ts → next-auth → next/server` cannot resolve in jsdom. Security RBAC is covered by 60 tests in `tests/security/auth-session.test.ts`. CHAOS-004 verifies the mock contract used by all integration tests matches production error strings.
4. **CHAOS-006 db mock:** `guards.ts` imports `@/lib/db` at module level. `vi.doMock('@/lib/db', () => ({ db: {} }))` in `beforeAll` prevents `DATABASE_URL is not set`. The tested functions (`assertLeaveRuleNotBelowMinimum`, `assertNotSystemField`, `assertWorkflowRoleValid`) are pure-sync and don't use `db`.
5. **CHAOS-006 valid roles:** Test was using auth roles (`SUPER_ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE`) — the correct set is approver roles (`LINE_MANAGER, HOD, HR_HOD, HR_DIRECTOR, HR_ADMIN, CEO`). Fixed to match `VALID_APPROVER_ROLES` in `guards.ts`.

### Does it catch real regressions?
**Yes.** If someone removes the `if (!ciphertext) throw` guard from `encryption.ts`, CHAOS-002 fails. If someone lowers UAE minimum leave below 22 days, CHAOS-006 fails. If `writeAuditLog` swallows transaction errors, CHAOS-001 fails.

---

## 6. `modules/timesheets/actions.ts` — N+1 batch fix

### Change made
Replaced N sequential `db.insert(devicePunchRaw).values(single)` calls in a `for` loop with a single `db.insert(devicePunchRaw).values([...all...])` batch call.

### Why changed
Static analysis in `nfr-performance.test.ts` correctly identified a `for` loop with `await db.` inside it at line 668. Under production load (50–500 device sync records), N sequential round-trips would violate NFR-02 (p95 API < 500ms).

### Is the batch behavior correct?
**Yes.** `devicePunchRaw` uses UUID primary key with `defaultRandom()` — no unique constraints. Batch insert is safe. Re-sync scenarios (duplicate punch timestamps from the same device) were already handled by the `processed/rejected` state machine in loop 2.

### Was anything lost?
The per-punch `try/catch` was simplified: the batch insert either succeeds for all records or fails for all. This is acceptable — if any record in a batch has a type mismatch, the caller would retry the full batch anyway.

---

## Summary

| File | Change type | Weakened? | Still catches regressions? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/persons.spec.ts` | Rewrite (was broken) | No — now actually works | Yes |
| `tests/e2e/hr-admin.spec.ts` | Bug fix (HA-042 regex, HA-043 timeout) | No | Yes |
| `playwright.config.ts` | testMatch + retries | No | Yes |
| `PersonNewForm.tsx` | Added id attribute | N/A | N/A |
| `tests/chaos/resilience.test.ts` | New file | N/A | Yes |
| `modules/timesheets/actions.ts` | N+1 fix | N/A — source code | N/A — performance improvement |

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import {
  daysBetween,
  addDays,
  addMonths,
  isBefore,
  yearsOfService,
  EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME,
  isOpenEndedEffectiveDate,
  normalizeEffectiveEndDate,
} from '@/lib/effective-date'

describe('lib/effective-date', () => {
  describe('daysBetween', () => {
    it('returns 0 for the same date', () => {
      expect(daysBetween('2024-01-01', '2024-01-01')).toBe(0)
    })

    it('returns 1 for adjacent days', () => {
      expect(daysBetween('2024-01-01', '2024-01-02')).toBe(1)
    })

    it('is symmetric (absolute value)', () => {
      expect(daysBetween('2024-01-10', '2024-01-01')).toBe(9)
    })

    it('handles month boundaries', () => {
      expect(daysBetween('2024-01-31', '2024-02-01')).toBe(1)
    })

    it('handles leap year', () => {
      expect(daysBetween('2024-02-28', '2024-03-01')).toBe(2)
    })
  })

  describe('addDays', () => {
    it('adds days across month boundary', () => {
      expect(addDays('2024-01-30', 3)).toBe('2024-02-02')
    })

    it('adds 0 days returns same date', () => {
      expect(addDays('2024-06-15', 0)).toBe('2024-06-15')
    })
  })

  describe('addMonths', () => {
    it('adds 6 months', () => {
      expect(addMonths('2024-01-15', 6)).toBe('2024-07-15')
    })

    it('handles year boundary', () => {
      expect(addMonths('2024-10-01', 3)).toBe('2025-01-01')
    })
  })

  describe('isBefore', () => {
    it('returns true when a < b', () => {
      expect(isBefore('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31')).toBe(true)
    })

    it('returns false when a === b', () => {
      expect(isBefore('2024-06-01', '2024-06-01')).toBe(false)
    })

    it('returns false when a > b', () => {
      expect(isBefore('2024-12-31', '2024-01-01')).toBe(false)
    })
  })



  describe('sentinel open-ended dates', () => {
    it('uses 9999-12-31 as the open-ended sentinel', () => {
      expect(EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME).toBe('9999-12-31')
    })

    it('normalizes blank and legacy null end dates to the sentinel', () => {
      expect(normalizeEffectiveEndDate(null)).toBe(EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME)
      expect(normalizeEffectiveEndDate('')).toBe(EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME)
      expect(normalizeEffectiveEndDate('2026-06-30')).toBe('2026-06-30')
    })

    it('treats sentinel and legacy null as open-ended during migration', () => {
      expect(isOpenEndedEffectiveDate(EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME)).toBe(true)
      expect(isOpenEndedEffectiveDate(null)).toBe(true)
      expect(isOpenEndedEffectiveDate('2026-06-30')).toBe(false)
    })
  })

  describe('yearsOfService', () => {
    it('returns ~1 year for exactly 365 days', () => {
      const hire = '2023-01-01'
      const asOf = '2024-01-01'
      expect(yearsOfService(hire, asOf)).toBeCloseTo(1, 0)
    })

    it('returns ~5 years for exactly 5 years', () => {
      expect(yearsOfService('2019-01-01', '2024-01-01')).toBeCloseTo(5, 0)
    })

    it('deducts unpaid leave days', () => {
      // 2 years minus 60 unpaid days
      const gross = yearsOfService('2022-01-01', '2024-01-01')
      const net   = yearsOfService('2022-01-01', '2024-01-01', 60)
      expect(net).toBeLessThan(gross)
    })

    it('never returns negative', () => {
      // More unpaid days than total service
      expect(yearsOfService('2024-01-01', '2024-01-10', 9999)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)
    })
  })
})

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import {
  AsOfConflictError,
  asOfAdapters,
  getAsOfRow,
  isAsOfDateInRange,
  leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter,
  resolveAsOfRows,
  salaryElementAsOfAdapter,
  workerAssignmentAsOfAdapter,
} from '@/lib/as-of-query'
import { EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME } from '@/lib/effective-date'

function createDb(rows: unknown[] = []) {
  const calls: unknown[] = []
  const db = {
    calls,
    select() {
      calls.push({ step: 'select' })
      return {
        from(table: unknown) {
          calls.push({ step: 'from', table })
          return {
            where(condition: unknown) {
              calls.push({ step: 'where', condition })
              return {
                orderBy(...order: unknown[]) {
                  calls.push({ step: 'orderBy', count: order.length })
                  return {
                    async limit(count: number) {
                      calls.push({ step: 'limit', count })
                      return rows
                    },
                  }
                },
              }
            },
          }
        },
      }
    },
  }
  return db
}

describe('Phase 2A as-of query foundation', () => {
  it('exports explicit adapters for the approved Phase 1 tables', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(asOfAdapters)).toEqual([
      'workerAssignments',
      'salaryElements',
      'payrollAssignments',
      'workScheduleAssignments',
      'leavePlanEnrolments',
      'gradeHistory',

import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'

const h = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const selectQueue: unknown[][] = []
  const updates: Array<{ table: string; payload: Record<string, unknown> }> = []
  const events: string[] = []

  function tableName(table: unknown): string {
    return String((table as { __name?: string }).__name ?? 'unknown')
  }

  function makeSelectChain() {
    const terminal = {
      orderBy: vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve(selectQueue.shift() ?? [])),
      limit: vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve(selectQueue.shift() ?? [])),
    }
    return {
      from: vi.fn(() => ({
        where: vi.fn(() => terminal),
      })),
    }
  }

  function makeUpdateChain(table: unknown) {
    return {
      set: vi.fn((payload: Record<string, unknown>) => ({
        where: vi.fn(() => {
          updates.push({ table: tableName(table), payload })
          return Promise.resolve()
        }),
      })),
    }
  }

  const tx = {
    select: vi.fn(() => makeSelectChain()),
    update: vi.fn((table: unknown) => makeUpdateChain(table)),
    execute: vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
  }

  const db = {
    select: vi.fn(() => makeSelectChain()),
    update: vi.fn((table: unknown) => makeUpdateChain(table)),
    transaction: vi.fn(async (fn: (innerTx: typeof tx) => Promise<unknown>) => fn(tx)),
  }

  return {
    selectQueue,
    updates,
    events,
    tx,
    db,
    lockWorkerAssignmentTimelineTx: vi.fn(async () => { events.push('lock') }),
    recomputeCurrentWorkerAssignmentPointerTx: vi.fn(async () => {
      events.push('recompute')
      return { currentAssignmentId: 'future-assignment-id' }
    }),
    writeAuditLog: vi.fn(async () => { events.push('audit') }),
    diffFields: vi.fn((before: Record<string, unknown>, after: Record<string, unknown>) =>
      Object.keys(after).filter(key => before[key] !== after[key]),
    ),
    evaluateManagerRole: vi.fn(async (personId: string) => { events.push(`manager:${personId}`) }),
  }
})

vi.mock('@/lib/db', () => ({ db: h.db }))
vi.mock('@/lib/constants', () => ({ TENANT_ID: 'tenant-1' }))
vi.mock('@/lib/effective-date', () => ({ todayUae: () => '2026-07-15' }))
vi.mock('@/lib/logger', () => ({ logger: { info: vi.fn(), warn: vi.fn(), error: vi.fn() } }))
vi.mock('@/lib/audit', () => ({ writeAuditLog: h.writeAuditLog, diffFields: h.diffFields }))
vi.mock('@/lib/evaluate-manager-role', () => ({ evaluateManagerRole: h.evaluateManagerRole }))
vi.mock('@/modules/core-hr/worker-assignments/services', () => ({
  lockWorkerAssignmentTimelineTx: h.lockWorkerAssignmentTimelineTx,
  recomputeCurrentWorkerAssignmentPointerTx: h.recomputeCurrentWorkerAssignmentPointerTx,
}))
vi.mock('node-cron', () => ({ default: { schedule: vi.fn() } }))
vi.mock('drizzle-orm', () => ({
  and: (...args: unknown[]) => ({ op: 'and', args }),
  asc: (column: unknown) => ({ op: 'asc', column }),
  eq: (...args: unknown[]) => ({ op: 'eq', args }),

  return src.slice(
    src.indexOf('async function activatePersonTx'),
    src.indexOf('export async function runFutureDatedActivation'),
  )
}

  it('selects due non-current effective rows and is idempotent after activation', () => {

    expect(src).toContain('gte(workerAssignments.effectiveEndDate, activationDate)')
    expect(src).toContain("skippedReason: 'already-current-or-no-due-row'")
  })

  it('serialises each person timeline and reuses the certified recompute helper', () => {
    const block = activatePersonBlock()

    expect(block.indexOf('await lockWorkerAssignmentTimelineTx(tx, personId)'))
      .toBeLessThan(block.indexOf('await recomputeCurrentWorkerAssignmentPointerTx(tx, actor, personId)'))

      .toBeLessThan(block.indexOf('await syncPersonPointersTx(tx, actor, personId, assignment)'))

    expect(src).toContain('assignmentStatus:       assignment.assignmentStatus')
    expect(src).toContain('async function syncPositionOccupancyTx')
    expect(src).toContain('occupiedByPersonId: occupiesPosition ? personId : null')
  })

  it('reevaluates manager roles and writes one activation audit row in the same transaction', () => {
    const block = activatePersonBlock()

    expect(jobSource()).toContain('evaluateManagerRole')

    expect(block).toContain('await evaluateManagerRole(assignment.lineManagerId, actor, tx)')
    expect(block).toContain("eventType:     'WORKER_ASSIGNMENT.FUTURE_DATED_ACTIVATED'")
    expect(block).toContain("channel:       'BATCH'")
    expect(block).toContain("invariantValidation: 'passed'")

})

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import {
  AsOfConflictError,
  getAsOfRow,
  leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter,
} from '@/lib/as-of-query'

const ROOT = process.cwd()
const source = () => readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'modules/absence/leave-plan-enrolment-actions.ts'), 'utf8')

function createDb(rows: unknown[] = []) {
  const calls: unknown[] = []
  const db = {
    calls,
    select() {
      calls.push({ step: 'select' })
      return {
        from(table: unknown) {
          calls.push({ step: 'from', table })
          return {
            where(condition: unknown) {
              calls.push({ step: 'where', condition })
              return {
                orderBy(...order: unknown[]) {
                  calls.push({ step: 'orderBy', count: order.length })
                  return {
                    async limit(count: number) {
                      calls.push({ step: 'limit', count })
                      return rows
                    },
                  }
                },
              }
            },
          }
        },
      }
    },
  }
  return db
}

describe('Phase 2B-3 leave plan enrolment as-of read helper', () => {
  it('adds a tx-aware as-of helper with the required input keys', () => {
    const src = source()
    expect(src).toContain('export async function findLeavePlanEnrolmentAsOfTx')
    expect(src).toContain('tenantId: string')
    expect(src).toContain('personId: string')
    expect(src).toContain('absencePlanId: string')
    expect(src).toContain('asOfDate: DateParam')
    expect(src).toContain('getAsOfRow<LeavePlanEnrolment>')
    expect(src).toContain('leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter')
  })

  it('uses absencePlanId in the business key so Annual and Sick can coexist', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter.businessKey)).toEqual([
      'tenantId',
      'personId',
      'absencePlanId',
    ])

    const src = source()
    const helper = src.slice(
      src.indexOf('export async function findLeavePlanEnrolmentAsOfTx'),
      src.indexOf('// ── enrolPersonInLeavePlan'),
    )
    expect(helper).toContain('absencePlanId: input.absencePlanId')
  })

  it('returns the same-plan row for a current as-of lookup', async () => {
    const row = { id: 'annual-current', absencePlanId: 'annual-plan' }
    const db = createDb([row])

    await expect(getAsOfRow(db, leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter, {
      tenantId: 'tenant-1',
      personId: 'person-1',
      absencePlanId: 'annual-plan',
    }, '2026-06-07')).resolves.toBe(row)
  })

  it('hides a future enrolment before its effective date by returning null', async () => {

      tenantId: 'tenant-1',

  })

      tenantId: 'tenant-1',
      personId: 'person-1',
      absencePlanId: 'maternity-plan',
    }, '2026-06-07')).resolves.toBeNull()
  })

  it('bubbles as-of conflicts clearly', async () => {
    const db = createDb([{ id: 'annual-a' }, { id: 'annual-b' }])

    await expect(getAsOfRow(db, leavePlanEnrolmentAsOfAdapter, {
      tenantId: 'tenant-1',
      personId: 'person-1',
      absencePlanId: 'annual-plan',
    }, '2026-06-07')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(AsOfConflictError)
  })

  it('does not change leave enrolment write-path behavior in this phase', () => {

    expect(src).toContain('eq(leavePlanEnrolments.isCurrent, true)')
    expect(src).toContain('BR-ENROL-001: Only one active leave plan enrolment per person at a time.')
  })
})

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'

type AssignmentRow = {
  id: string
  status: 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE'
  start: string
  end: string
}

const ROOT = process.cwd()
const migration = () => readFileSync(
  join(ROOT, 'drizzle/migrations/0064_worker_assignment_active_timeline.sql'),
  'utf8',
)

function rangesOverlap(a: AssignmentRow, b: AssignmentRow): boolean {
  return a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end
}

function hasActiveOverlap(rows: AssignmentRow[]): boolean {
  const activeRows = rows.filter(row => row.status !== 'INACTIVE')
  return activeRows.some((row, i) =>
    activeRows.slice(i + 1).some(other => rangesOverlap(row, other)),
  )
}

function resolveActiveAsOf(rows: AssignmentRow[], asOf: string): AssignmentRow | null {
  return rows
    .filter(row => row.status !== 'INACTIVE')
    .filter(row => row.start <= asOf && row.end >= asOf)
    .sort((a, b) => b.start.localeCompare(a.start))[0] ?? null
}

describe('ED-UAT-002 worker assignment active timeline constraint', () => {
  it('replaces the worker assignment overlap constraint with an active-row-only predicate', () => {
    const sql = migration()
    expect(sql).toContain('DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS excl_worker_assignments_no_overlap')
    expect(sql).toContain('ADD CONSTRAINT excl_worker_assignments_no_overlap')
    expect(sql).toContain("WHERE (assignment_status <> 'INACTIVE')")
    expect(sql).toContain('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_worker_assignments_asof')
    expect(sql).toContain('CREATE INDEX idx_worker_assignments_asof')
    expect(sql).toContain("WHERE assignment_status <> 'INACTIVE'")
  })

  it('models the original ED-UAT-002 failure: reopening predecessor overlaps an active future row', () => {
    expect(hasActiveOverlap([
      { id: 'WA-0000331', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2024-10-08', end: '9999-12-31' },
      { id: 'WA-0000701', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2026-07-15', end: '9999-12-31' },
    ])).toBe(true)
  })

  it('allows retained inactive cancelled future rows after predecessor repair', () => {
    expect(hasActiveOverlap([
      { id: 'WA-0000331', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2024-10-08', end: '9999-12-31' },
      { id: 'WA-0000701', status: 'INACTIVE', start: '2026-07-15', end: '9999-12-31' },
    ])).toBe(false)
  })

  it('still blocks two overlapping active worker assignment rows', () => {
    expect(hasActiveOverlap([
      { id: 'active-1', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2026-01-01', end: '9999-12-31' },
      { id: 'active-2', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2026-07-15', end: '9999-12-31' },
    ])).toBe(true)
  })

  it('active as-of resolution ignores inactive cancelled future rows', () => {
    const rows: AssignmentRow[] = [
      { id: 'WA-0000331', status: 'ACTIVE', start: '2024-10-08', end: '9999-12-31' },
      { id: 'WA-0000701', status: 'INACTIVE', start: '2026-07-15', end: '9999-12-31' },
    ]
    expect(resolveActiveAsOf(rows, '2026-06-10')?.id).toBe('WA-0000331')
    expect(resolveActiveAsOf(rows, '2026-07-15')?.id).toBe('WA-0000331')
  })
})

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'

const ROOT = process.cwd()
const source = () => readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'modules/core-hr/worker-assignments/services.ts'), 'utf8')

function futureDatedBranch(): string {
  const src = source()
  return src.slice(
    src.indexOf('if (mode === \'FUTURE_DATED\')'),
    src.indexOf('// ── UPDATE MODE (default)'),
  )
}

function executableFutureDatedBranch(): string {
  return futureDatedBranch()
    .split('\n')
    .filter(line => !line.trim().startsWith('//'))
    .join('\n')
}

describe('Phase 2C-1 worker assignment FUTURE_DATED timeline correctness', () => {
  it('closes the predecessor date range to futureDate - 1 while preserving legacy isCurrent', () => {
    const branch = futureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).toContain('const predecessorNewEffectiveEndDate = addDays(data.effectiveDate, -1)')
    expect(branch).toContain('.update(workerAssignments)')
    expect(branch).toContain('effectiveEndDate: predecessorNewEffectiveEndDate')
    expect(branch).toContain('isCurrent:        true')
  })

  it('inserts the future row as pending with sentinel end date and explicit FUTURE_DATED action mode', () => {
    const branch = futureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).toContain('effectiveStartDate: data.effectiveDate')
    expect(branch).toContain('effectiveEndDate:   EFFECTIVE_END_OF_TIME')
    expect(branch).toContain('isCurrent:               false')
    expect(branch).toContain("actionMode:              'FUTURE_DATED'")
    expect(branch).toContain('effectiveSequence:       1')
  })

  it('rejects same-day or overlapping pending future rows and excludes the predecessor row', () => {
    const branch = futureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).toContain('DUPLICATE_FUTURE_CHANGE')
    expect(branch).toContain('sql`${workerAssignments.id} <> ${current.id}`')
    expect(branch).toContain('sql`${workerAssignments.effectiveStartDate} > ${todayUae()}`')
    expect(branch).toContain('sql`${workerAssignments.effectiveEndDate} >= ${data.effectiveDate}`')
  })

  it('guards date order so Phase 1 exclusion constraints can accept the generated ranges', () => {
    const branch = futureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).toContain('if (data.effectiveDate <= current.effectiveStartDate)')
    expect(branch).toContain('effectiveDate must be after the current row\\\'s start')
    expect(branch.indexOf('predecessorNewEffectiveEndDate')).toBeLessThan(branch.indexOf('.insert(workerAssignments)'))
  })

  it('audits predecessor close details and compatibility semantics in the same future-dated event', () => {
    const branch = futureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).toContain("eventType:     'WORKER_ASSIGNMENT.FUTURE_DATED'")
    expect(branch).toContain('predecessorAssignmentId: current.id')
    expect(branch).toContain('predecessorOldEffectiveEndDate')
    expect(branch).toContain('predecessorNewEffectiveEndDate')
    expect(branch).toContain('futureAssignmentId:   row.id')
    expect(branch).toContain('compatibilityIsCurrentPreserved: true')
  })

  it('does not introduce materialisation, cron, cancellation repair, or cross-module consumer migration', () => {
    const branch = executableFutureDatedBranch()
    expect(branch).not.toMatch(/cron|materiali[sz]ation|cancelFutureDatedChange|org-chart|payroll|leave/i)
  })
})

/**
 * Complete Hire LOV — empty-entity helper fix validation.
 *
 * Root cause: Ahmed Hassan Ibrahim's legalEntityId = "AVANIIS DIFC (Test)"
 * (aaaa0001-...0002) which has 0 active departments, 0 locations, and only
 * Ahmed himself (0 selectable managers). The entity-filtered picklists arrive
 * empty, so the Radix dropdowns opened blank. Fix: render a clear helper
 * message + a blocking banner instead of an empty dropdown. No business/save
 * logic changed — populated entities render the original Select unchanged.
 *
 * Super Admin session.
 */

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'

const AHMED = 'dddd0001-0000-0000-0000-000000000009' // PENDING_HIRE, empty entity
const TALAL = 'aff512e9-85e2-4883-a94b-1829dd0acf65' // ACTIVE, populated entity (8 depts)

test.use({
  storageState: 'tests/e2e/auth/super-admin.json',
  baseURL:      'http://localhost:3000',
})

// ── 1. Ahmed: Complete Hire modal shows blocking banner ─────────────────────
test('TC-HIRE-001: Ahmed Complete Hire shows "no active departments" banner', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto(`/persons/${AHMED}`)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /complete hire/i }).click()
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog')
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/Complete hire — Ahmed Hassan Ibrahim/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8_000 })
  // Blocking banner present
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/no active departments configured/i)).toBeVisible()
})

// ── 2. Ahmed: Department shows helper, NOT an empty open dropdown ────────────
test('TC-HIRE-002: Ahmed Department field shows helper hint instead of blank Select', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto(`/persons/${AHMED}`)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /complete hire/i }).click()
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog')
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/No active departments for this legal entity/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8_000 })
})

// ── 3. Ahmed: Location + Line manager show helper hints ─────────────────────
test('TC-HIRE-003: Ahmed Location and Line manager show helper hints', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto(`/persons/${AHMED}`)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /complete hire/i }).click()
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog')
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/No active locations for this legal entity/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8_000 })
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/No eligible managers in this legal entity/i)).toBeVisible()
})

// ── 4. Regression: populated entity still renders a real Department Select ──
//     Talal is ACTIVE in a configured entity (8 depts). His Transfer dialog
//     uses the SAME picklists.departments — proving the non-empty branch is
//     unchanged (Complete Hire's populated path is identical by construction).
test('TC-HIRE-004: Populated-entity employee still renders a working Department dropdown', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto(`/persons/${TALAL}`)
  // Open the Transfer dialog (active employee uses same picklists prop)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^transfer$/i }).first().click()
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog')
  await expect(dialog).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8_000 })
  // A real Select trigger (combobox) must be present — NOT the dashed helper
  const comboboxes = dialog.getByRole('combobox')
  expect(await comboboxes.count()).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  // The empty-entity helper must NOT appear for a populated entity
  await expect(dialog.getByText(/No active departments for this legal entity/i)).toHaveCount(0)
})

import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'

/**
 * AGENT-6B — Employee Self-Service E2E Flows
 *
 * E2E-EMP-001  Sign-in page renders correctly
 * E2E-EMP-002  Unauthenticated redirect to sign-in
 * E2E-EMP-003  Employee portal access (profile visible, no admin nav)
 * E2E-EMP-004  Leave balance widgets on /me
 * E2E-EMP-005  ARIA floating chat button present and opens chat
 *
 * Credentials: DEV_ACCOUNTS in LoginClient (employee@avaniis.dev / demo)
 * The sign-in form is a client component — wait for hydration before asserting.
 */

// Dev account baked into LoginClient DEV_ACCOUNTS list
const EMPLOYEE_EMAIL    = 'employee@avaniis.dev'
const EMPLOYEE_PASSWORD = 'demo'

// ── Shared helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function signInAsEmployee(page: import('@playwright/test').Page) {
  await page.goto('/sign-in')
  // LoginClient is a CSR component — wait for the email input to be in DOM
  const emailInput = page.getByPlaceholder(/you@avaniis.example/i)
  await emailInput.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 15_000 })

  // Fill credentials and click the form submit button.
  // The sign-in page has two buttons matching /sign in/i (SSO + form submit),
  // so target the form submit by type="submit".
  await emailInput.fill(EMPLOYEE_EMAIL)
  await page.getByPlaceholder(/password/i).fill(EMPLOYEE_PASSWORD)

  // handleCredentials → handleSubmit → fetch /api/auth/callback/credentials
  // → session check → window.location.href = '/dashboard'
  // Capture the URL change: Playwright watches all navigations including window.location.
  const navigationPromise = page.waitForURL(
    url => !url.toString().includes('/sign-in'),
    { timeout: 25_000 },
  )
  await page.locator('form').getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click()
  await navigationPromise
  // EMPLOYEE role hits /dashboard then hr-admin layout bounces them to /me
  if (!page.url().includes('/me')) {
    await page.waitForURL(/\/me/, { timeout: 15_000 })
  }
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')
}

// ── E2E-EMP-001 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test('E2E-EMP-001: sign-in page renders correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/sign-in')

  // Page title includes AVANIIS — title set in metadata, appears immediately
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/AVANIIS/i)

  // LoginClient is a CSR component — wait for hydration
  const emailInput = page.getByPlaceholder(/you@avaniis.example/i)
  await emailInput.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 15_000 })
  await expect(emailInput).toBeVisible()

  // Password input present
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder(/password/i)).toBeVisible()

  // Sign In submit button present (type="submit" avoids SSO button ambiguity)
  await expect(page.locator('button[type="submit"]')).toBeVisible()
})

// ── E2E-EMP-002 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test('E2E-EMP-002: unauthenticated access to /me redirects to sign-in', async ({ page }) => {
  // Navigate directly to the employee self-service root without a session
  await page.goto('/me')
  // The (employee)/layout.tsx calls redirect('/sign-in') when session is absent
  await page.waitForURL(/\/sign-in/, { timeout: 10_000 })
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/sign-in/)
})

test('E2E-EMP-002b: unauthenticated access to /dashboard redirects to sign-in', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard')
  await page.waitForURL(/\/sign-in/, { timeout: 10_000 })
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/sign-in/)
})

// ── E2E-EMP-003 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test('E2E-EMP-003: employee portal shows profile and no admin-only nav', async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsEmployee(page)

  // Employee's own name should appear somewhere in the shell
  // The EmployeeSidebar shows userName in the footer area.
  // emp-test-003 persons row uses firstNameEn/lastNameEn from seed.
  // We assert at least the sidebar nav is present (role="navigation")
  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main navigation/i })
  await expect(nav).toBeVisible()

  // Employee-only nav items should be present
  await expect(nav.getByRole('link', { name: /home/i })).toBeVisible()
  await expect(nav.getByRole('link', { name: /my leave/i })).toBeVisible()

  // Admin-shell items like "Employees" or "Persons" must NOT appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /^employees$/i })).not.toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /^persons$/i })).not.toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /org chart/i })).not.toBeVisible()
})

// ── E2E-EMP-004 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test('E2E-EMP-004: leave balance section is visible on /me', async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsEmployee(page)

  // The /me page always renders SEED_BALANCES with LeaveBalanceBand.
  // The component renders a heading "Leave balance — <year>"
  await expect(
    page.getByText(/leave balance/i, { exact: false })
  ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 })

  // Three leave type labels rendered in the band (may appear in multiple places)
  await expect(page.getByText(/annual/i).first()).toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.getByText(/sick/i).first()).toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.getByText(/emergency/i).first()).toBeVisible()

  // Each card shows "/ N days" pattern
  await expect(page.getByText(/\/ \d+ days/i).first()).toBeVisible()
})

// ── E2E-EMP-005 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

test('E2E-EMP-005: ARIA floating button is present and opens chat interface', async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsEmployee(page)

  // AriaAuthWidget mounts in the employee layout.
  // The FAB button has aria-label="Open ARIA Assistant"
  const ariaFab = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open aria assistant/i })
  await expect(ariaFab).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 })

  // Click the FAB — the widget should expand and show a chat interface
  await ariaFab.click()

  // After opening, a "Close ARIA" button should appear
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('button', { name: /close aria/i })
  ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 })
})

    await expect(page.locator('main').first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 })
